## 2 Discretely self-similar characteristic data

The characteristic initial data are given by $r,\Omega,\phi$ which satisfy Raychaudhuri’s equations (1.8) on $C_{0}^{-}$ and (1.9) on $C_{0}^{+}.$ In this section we set up suitable characteristic initial data, which are consistent with ingoing discrete self-similarity along $C_{0}^{-}$ and asymptotic flatness along $C_{0}^{+}.$

### 2.1 Underlying manifold and gauge conditions

We will consider the maximal globally hyperbolic development of data imposed on the bifurcate double null cones $C_{0}^{-}=\{-1\leq u<0\}\times\{v=0\}$ and $C_{0}^{+}=\{u=-1\}\times\{0\leq v<\infty\}$ . The bifurcation sphere is $p=\{u=-1\}\times\{v=0\}.$ We will denote the future domain of dependence of $C_{0}^{-}\cup_{p}C_{0}^{+}$ with $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{ext}}=\{-1\leq u<0\}\times\{0\leq v<\infty\}$ .

On the incoming cone $C_{0}^{-}$ we impose

$$ r(u,0)=-u. $$

This can be interpreted as choosing the gauge condition $\partial_{u}r=-1$ along $C_{0}^{-}$ and $r(p)=1$ . We also impose that $\phi(p)=0$ .

On the outgoing cone $C_{0}^{+}$ we impose the gauge

$$ \partial_{v}\Omega^{2}=0. $$

This fixes the gauge upon specifying $\Omega^{2}(p)$ which will be done later. We are now in the position of defining characteristic data with ingoing discrete self-similarity.

### 2.2 Characteristic data with ingoing discrete self-similarity

#### Definition 2.1 (Characteristic data with ingoing discrete self-similarity).

Let $N>0$ be a regularity index for the tangential derivatives. We say that the seed $\phi(\cdot,0):C_{0}^{-}\to\mathbb{R}$ , $\phi(0,\cdot)\colon C_{0}^{+}\to\mathbb{R}$ with $\phi(p)=0$ gives rise to a $C^{N}$ -regular characteristic data set on $C_{0}^{-}\cup_{p}C_{0}^{+}$ with ingoing discrete self-similarity if there exist constants $\Delta>0$ , $0<\kappa<1$ , and $C_{data}>0$ such that upon specifying

$$ \Omega^{2}(p)=\frac{1}{1-\kappa} $$

and imposing the gauge conditions from Section 2.1, the following conditions hold:

- 1. The scalar field satisfies $\phi(\cdot,0)\in C^{N+1}(C_{0}^{-})$ and $\phi(0,\cdot)\in C^{N+1}(C_{0}^{+})$ .

- 2. The scalar field is discretely self-similar on $C_{0}^{-}$ , i.e.,

$$ \phi(e^{-\Delta}u,0)=\phi(u,0). $$

(2.3)

- 3. The constant $\kappa$ satisfies

$$ \kappa=\frac{F(-e^{-\Delta})}{\Delta}, $$

(2.4) where

$$ F(u)\doteq\int_{-1}^{u}(-u^{\prime})\big(\partial_{u}\phi(u^{\prime},0)\big)^{2}du^{\prime}. $$

(2.5)

- 4. The scalar field satisfies the self-similar bounds

$$ \ |\phi(u,0)|\leq C_{data}\sqrt{\kappa},\ |\partial_{u}\phi(u,0)|\leq C_{data}\sqrt{\kappa}|u|^{-1} $$

(2.6) on $C_{0}^{-}$ .

- 5. The mass aspect ratio $\mu\doteq\frac{2m}{r}$ is discretely self-similar on $C_{0}^{-}$ , i.e.,

$$ \mu(e^{-\Delta}u,0)=\mu(u,0). $$

(2.7)

- 6. The first transverse derivatives of the scalar field and of the radiation field are discretely self-similar along $C_{0}^{-}$

$$ \frac{\partial_{v}(r\phi)}{\partial_{v}r}(e^{-\Delta}u,0)=\frac{\partial_{v}(r\phi)}{\partial_{v}r}(u,0) $$

(2.8) and

$$ \frac{\partial_{v}\phi}{\partial_{v}r}(e^{-\Delta}u,0)=e^{\Delta}\frac{\partial_{v}\phi}{\partial_{v}r}(u,0). $$

(2.9)

- 7. The scalar field satisfies the asymptotically flat conditions on $C_{0}^{+}$

$$ \big|\partial_{v}\phi(-1,v)\big|\leq C_{data}\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot\frac{1}{(1+v)^{2}},\quad\big|\partial_{v}^{2}\phi(-1,v)\big|\leq C_{data}\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot\frac{1}{(1+v)^{3}}. $$

(2.10)

#### Remark 2.2.

The equation (2.4) can also be regarded as a definition of $\kappa$ which measures the size of $\phi$ along $C_{0}^{-}$ . In our construction, we will take $\kappa$ to be a small quantity.

#### Remark 2.3.

Note that $\Omega^{2}$ and the transverse derivatives $\partial_{v}r$ and $\partial_{v}\phi$ along $C_{0}^{-}$ are determined by their values at the bifurcation sphere $p$ and (1.6)–(1.8). We will prove in Lemma 2.7 and Lemma 2.8 in Section 2.3 that for discretely self-similar data as in Definition 2.1, the values $\partial_{v}r(p)$ and $\partial_{v}\phi(p)$ are rigid.

The statement that there exist non-trivial characteristic data with ingoing discrete self-similarity as defined in Definition 2.1 is the content of the following proposition, which will be proved in Section 2.4.

#### Proposition 2.4.

For any $\Delta>0$ , there exists a $C_{data}=C_{data}(\Delta)>0$ such that for any $\kappa>0$ , and $N\geq 1$ , there exists a non-trivial seed function $\phi\colon C_{0}^{-}\cup_{p}C_{0}^{+}\to\mathbb{R}$ giving rise to $C^{k}$ -regular characteristic data with ingoing self-similarity as defined in Definition 2.1.

### 2.3 Consequences of imposing discrete self-similarity

In Section 2 we use the following convention. For non-negative quantities $A$ and $B$ , we write $A\lesssim B$ if there exists a constant $\tilde{C}>0$ only depending on $C_{data}$ and $\Delta$ from Definition 2.1 such that $A\leq\tilde{C}B$ . We will also write “for sufficiently small $0<\kappa\ll 1$ ” if there exists a constant $\kappa_{0}>0$ sufficiently small and only depending on $C_{data}$ , $\Delta$ from Definition 2.1 such that $\kappa$ satisfies $0<\kappa\leq\kappa_{0}$ .

#### 2.3.1 Estimates and rigidity along the ingoing cone $C_{0}^{-}$

As a consequence of discrete self-similarity along $C_{0}^{-}$ , we prove rigidity for the lapse $\Omega^{2}$ in Lemma 2.5 and Lemma 2.6. We also prove rigidity for $\partial_{v}r$ and $\partial_{v}\phi$ on $C_{0}^{-}$ in Lemma 2.7 and Lemma 2.8, which in particular determines the outgoing data on $C_{0}^{+}$ to first order at $p.$

#### Lemma 2.5.

Consider discretely self-similar data as in Definition 2.1. Then, the function $F$ as defined in (2.5) satisfies

$$ F(-1)=0,\quad F(e^{-n\Delta}u)=F(u)+n\kappa\Delta. $$

for $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and

$$ \sup_{u\in[-1,0)}\Big|\frac{F(u)}{\log|u|}\Big|\lesssim\kappa,\quad\left|\frac{d}{du}F(u)\right|\lesssim\kappa|u|^{-1},\ \left|\log\big(|u|^{-\kappa}e^{-F(u)}\big)\right|\lesssim\kappa. $$

#### Proof.

We compute

$$ \displaystyle F(u) \displaystyle=\int_{-1}^{u}(-u^{\prime})(\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}du^{\prime}=\int_{-e^{-\Delta}}^{e^{-\Delta}u}(-e^{\Delta}u^{\prime})(e^{-\Delta}\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}e^{\Delta}du^{\prime} \displaystyle=\int_{-1}^{e^{-\Delta}u}(-u^{\prime})(\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}du^{\prime}-\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}(-u^{\prime})(\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}du^{\prime}=F(e^{-\Delta}u)-\kappa\Delta, $$

where we used a change of variables, (2.3) and (2.4). Iterating this yields (2.11). The bounds (2.12) are a direct consequence of (2.6) and (2.11). ∎

#### Lemma 2.6.

Consider self-similar data as in Definition 2.1. Then, the lapse $\Omega^{2}(u,0)$ on $C_{0}^{-}$ is uniquely determined as

$$ \Omega^{2}(u,0)=\frac{1}{1-\kappa}e^{-F(u)}, $$

where $F$ is defined in (2.5). In particular,

$$ \Omega^{2}(e^{-\Delta n}u,0)=e^{-n\Delta\kappa}\Omega^{2}(u,0). $$

#### Proof.

By our gauge condition on $C_{0}^{-}$ we have $\partial_{u}r=-1$ . Thus, (1.8) reads

$$ \partial_{u}(\Omega^{-2})=-u\Omega^{-2}(\partial_{u}\phi)^{2} $$

or

$$ \partial_{u}\log\Omega^{2}=u(\partial_{u}\phi)^{2} $$

which shows (2.13) upon integration and using (2.5). ∎

#### Lemma 2.7.

Consider discretely self-similar data as in Definition 2.1. Then, the following holds:

- 1. The quantity $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r$ is discretely self-similar on $C_{0}^{-}$ :

$$ \Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)=\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(e^{-\Delta}u,0). $$

(2.16)

- 2. The transverse derivative $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)$ at the bifurcation sphere $p$ is determined by the data on $C_{0}^{-}$ and satisfies

$$ \Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)=\frac{1}{4-4e^{-\Delta(1+\kappa)}}\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}. $$

(2.17)

- 3. The transverse derivative $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)$ along $C_{0}^{-}$ is determined by the data on $C_{0}^{-}$ and given as

$$ \Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)=\frac{e^{F(u)}}{-u}\cdot\bigg(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)-\frac{1}{4}\int_{-1}^{u}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\bigg). $$

(2.18)

- 4. For $0<\kappa\ll 1$ sufficiently small, we have the bounds $\displaystyle\sup_{u\in[-1,0)}\big|4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r-1\big|\lesssim\kappa,\quad\sup_{u\in[-1,0)}|\mu|\lesssim\kappa.$ (2.19)

#### Proof.

The constraint (2.16) follows from

$$ \mu=\frac{2m}{r}=1+4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{u}r\partial_{v}r=1-4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r $$

on $C_{0}^{-}$ and the imposed discrete self-similarity condition (2.7) for $\mu$ .

We now use (1.7), (2.15) and $\partial_{u}r=-1$ to compute

$$ \displaystyle\partial_{u}(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r) \displaystyle=\partial_{u}\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r+\Omega^{-2}\left(\frac{-\Omega^{2}}{4r}-\frac{\partial_{u}r\partial_{v}r}{r}\right) \displaystyle=\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r\left(\partial_{u}\log\Omega^{-2}-\frac{\partial_{u}r}{r}\right)-\frac{1}{4r} \displaystyle=\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r\left(-u(\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}-\frac{1}{u}\right)+\frac{1}{4u}. $$

Using the definition of $F$ we rewrite the above as

$$ \partial_{u}\left(e^{-F(u)+\int_{-1}^{u}\frac{1}{u^{\prime}}du^{\prime}}\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r\right)=\frac{1}{4u}e^{-F(u)+\int_{-1}^{u}\frac{1}{u^{\prime}}du^{\prime}}=-\frac{1}{4}e^{-F(u)}. $$

We integrate from $u=-1$ to $u$ to obtain

$$ (-u)e^{-F(u)}\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u)-\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)=\int_{-1}^{u}-\frac{1}{4}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}. $$

Solving for $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r$ yields (2.18). In order to obtain the formula for $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)$ we use the periodicity of $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r$ and obtain from (2.22) that $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)$ has to satisfy

$$ \Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)(e^{\Delta(-\kappa-1)}-1)=\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}-\frac{1}{4}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}. $$

Solving for $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)$ gives (2.17).

To prove the bounds in (2.19), we first observe the bounds

$$ \sup_{u\in[-1,-e^{-\Delta}]}|F|\lesssim\kappa,\quad\sup_{u\in[-1,-e^{-\Delta}]}|e^{-F}-1|\lesssim\kappa,\quad\text{ and }\quad|e^{-\Delta\kappa}-1|\lesssim\kappa. $$

Thus, using (2.17) we obtain

$$ \left|4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)-1\right|=\left|\frac{1}{1-e^{-\Delta-\Delta\kappa}}\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}e^{F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}-1\right|\lesssim\left|\frac{1}{1-e^{-\Delta}}\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}du^{\prime}-1\right|+\kappa=\kappa. $$

Using the above estimates, (2.18) and (2.16) we obtain that

$$ \displaystyle\sup_{u\in[-1,0)}|4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)-1| \displaystyle=\sup_{u\in[-1,-e^{-\Delta}]}|4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)-1| \displaystyle=\sup_{u\in[-1,-e^{-\Delta}]}\frac{e^{F(u)}}{-u}\left|4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)-\int_{-1}^{u}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}+ue^{-F(u)}\right|\lesssim\kappa. $$

The bound on $\mu$ follows from the above and (2.20) which concludes the proof. ∎

Analogously to the rigidity for $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)$ from Lemma 2.7 will now show that the discrete self-similarity for $\frac{\partial_{v}(r\phi)}{\partial_{v}r}$ along $C_{0}^{-}$ constrains $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi$ at the bifurcation sphere $p$ .

#### Lemma 2.8.

Consider discretely self-similar data as in Definition 2.1. Then, the following holds:

- 1. The quantity $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)$ is discretely self-similar on $C_{0}^{-}$

$$ \Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(u,0)=\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(e^{-\Delta}u,0). $$

(2.24)

- 2. The transverse derivative $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)$ at the bifurcation sphere $p$ is determined by the data on $C_{0}^{-}$ and satisfies

$$ \Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)=-\frac{e^{\kappa\Delta}}{1-e^{\kappa\Delta}}\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}\frac{e^{-F(u^{\prime})}}{-4u^{\prime}}\mu(u^{\prime})\phi(u^{\prime})du^{\prime}. $$

(2.25)

- 3. The transverse derivative $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(u,0)$ along $C_{0}^{-}$ is determined by the data on $C_{0}^{-}$ and given as

$$ \Omega^{-2}(u,0)\partial_{v}(r\phi)(u,0)=e^{F(u)}\left(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)-\int_{-1}^{u}\frac{e^{-F(u^{\prime})}}{-4u^{\prime}}\mu(u^{\prime})\phi(u^{\prime})du^{\prime}\right). $$

(2.26)

- 4. For $0<\kappa\ll 1$ sufficiently small, we have the bound

$$ \big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)\big|\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa}. $$

(2.27)

#### Proof.

The first statement (2.24) is a direct consequence of (2.8) and (2.16).

We now write (1.7) as

$$ \partial_{u}\partial_{v}(r\phi)=-\frac{m\Omega^{2}}{2r^{2}}\phi $$

which, after integration and multiplication by $\Omega^{-2}$ , gives

$$ \Omega^{-2}(u,0)\partial_{v}(r\phi)(u,0)=\Omega^{-2}(u,0)\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)-\Omega^{-2}(u,0)\int_{-1}^{u}\frac{\Omega^{2}(u^{\prime},0)}{-4u}\mu\phi du^{\prime}. $$

Evaluating the above at $u=-e^{-\Delta}$ and using (2.24) gives

$$ \Omega^{-2}(p)\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)=\frac{\Omega^{-2}(-e^{-\Delta},0)}{\Omega^{-2}(p)}\Omega^{-2}(p)\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)-\Omega^{-2}(-e^{-\Delta},0)\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}\frac{\Omega^{2}(u^{\prime},0)}{-4u^{\prime}}\mu\phi du^{\prime}. $$

Solving for $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)$ and using (2.13) yields (2.25). Similarly, we obtain

$$ \Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(u,0)=e^{F(u)}\left(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)-\int_{-1}^{u}\frac{e^{-F(u^{\prime})}}{-4u^{\prime}}\mu\phi du^{\prime}\right). $$

To prove (2.27) we first note that

$$ |\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)|\lesssim\frac{1}{\kappa\Delta}\sup_{u\in[-1,-e^{-\Delta}]}|\mu\phi|\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa}, $$

where we used (2.6) and (2.19). Using the periodicity of $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(u,0)$ and the bounds on $\phi$ and $\mu$ as we did to control $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)$ , we obtain (2.27) which concludes the proof. ∎

#### Remark 2.9.

In Definition 2.1 we require the first transverse derivative of the geometry and scalar field to be discretely self-similar. Analogously, one can define discretely self-similar profiles of higher order $n\geq 1$ . This would impose $n-1$ additional constraints on the higher-order transverse derivatives of the scalar field $\partial_{v}^{i}\phi|_{p}$ and on the radius $\partial_{v}^{i}r|_{p}$ for $i\leq n$ , analogously to Lemma 2.7 and Lemma 2.8.

#### 2.3.2 Estimates along the outgoing cone

We note that along the outgoing cone, we have that

$$ \Omega^{2}(-1,v)=\frac{1}{1-\kappa} $$

which is a consequence of (2.2) and the gauge condition (2.1). The self-similarity imposed on the scalar field means that

$$ \partial_{v}\phi(p)=\frac{-e^{\kappa\Delta}}{(1-\kappa)(1-e^{\kappa\Delta})}\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}\frac{e^{-F(u^{\prime})}}{-4u^{\prime}}\mu(u^{\prime})\phi(u^{\prime})du^{\prime} $$

where we recall that $\phi(p)=0$ .

#### Remark 2.10.

Our arguments also apply if we only require the regularity for $\phi$ to be $C^{1,\gamma}_{v}\big([0,\infty)\big),$ where $\gamma=2\kappa/(1-\kappa).$ We notice that this is the same regularity exponent as in [RS23]. However, while in the examples of [Chr94] and [RS23] restricting the regularity of the spacetime was essential in the construction of the exterior solution, in our case we can already achieve this for a smooth scalar field.

The above choices determine $r$ on $C_{0}^{+}$ by the Raychaudhuri equation (1.9) and the constraints at $p$ :

$$ \begin{cases}\partial_{v}^{2}r=-r(\partial_{v}\phi)^{2}\\
r(p)=1,\ \partial_{v}r(p)=\frac{1}{(1-\kappa)(4-4e^{-\Delta(1+\kappa)})}\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}.\end{cases} $$

We have completed the setup for the characteristic initial data on $C_{0}^{+}.$ Next, we prove estimates on $C_{0}^{+}$ for all the relevant quantities that will be of use later in the proof.

#### Lemma 2.11.

Consider discretely self-similar data as in Definition 2.1. Then, for $0<\kappa\ll 1$ sufficiently small, we have

$$ \bigg|r(-1,v)-1-\partial_{v}r(p)v\bigg|\lesssim\kappa v $$

and

$$ \bigg|\partial_{v}r(-1,v)-\partial_{v}r(p)\bigg|\lesssim\kappa. $$

#### Proof.

We denote $v_{*}=\sup\big\{v\colon\partial_{v}r>0\text{ on }[0,v]\big\},$ and we prove that $v_{*}=\infty.$ Since $\partial_{v}^{2}r(-1,v)<0,$ we have the bound $0\leq\partial_{v}r(-1,v)\leq\partial_{v}r(p)\leq 2$ on $[0,v_{*}),$ which implies that $1\leq r(-1,v)\leq 1+2v$ . From (1.9) get the bound on $[0,v_{*})$ :

$$ \big|\partial_{v}^{2}r(-1,v)\big|\lesssim\kappa\frac{1+2v}{(1+v)^{4}}. $$

We integrate this bound from 0 to obtain that (2.34) holds for all $v\in[0,v_{*}).$ Taking $\kappa$ sufficiently small, we obtain that $v_{*}=\infty$ as desired. Finally, we use (2.34) and the fundamental theorem of calculus to get (2.33). ∎

Next, we prove the following estimate for $\partial_{u}r$ :

#### Lemma 2.12.

Consider discretely self-similar data as in Definition 2.1. Then, for $0<\kappa\ll 1$ sufficiently small, we have

$$ \big|\partial_{u}r(-1,v)+1\big|\lesssim\kappa\frac{v}{v+1} $$

#### Proof.

We rewrite (1.6) as

$$ \partial_{v}\partial_{u}r^{2}=-\frac{1}{2}\Omega^{2} $$

and integrating along on $\{u=-1\}$ gives

$$ r\partial_{u}r+1=-\frac{v}{4(1-\kappa)}, $$

where we have also used the gauge condition (2.32). We can rewrite this equation on $\{u=-1\}$ as

$$ r(\partial_{u}r+1)=r-1-\frac{v}{4(1-\kappa)}=\bigg(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)-\frac{1}{4}\bigg)\frac{v}{1-\kappa}+O(\kappa v)=O(\kappa v), $$

where we also used (2.19) and (2.33). We then divide by $r$ which concludes the proof. ∎

The bounds that we proved so far on the initial data imply the smallness of the Hawking mass:

#### Lemma 2.13.

Consider discretely self-similar data as in Definition 2.1. Then,

$$ m(-1,v)\lesssim\kappa $$

for all $v\in[0,\infty).$

#### Proof.

From $m=\frac{1}{2}\mu r$ and the bound (2.19) we directly obtain $m(p)\lesssim\kappa$ . Plugging the bounds that we proved above for the initial data, we obtain that

$$ 0\leq\partial_{v}m\lesssim\frac{\kappa}{(1+v)^{2}} $$

which shows Lemma 2.13 upon integration. ∎

We also prove the following estimate for $\partial_{u}\phi:$

#### Lemma 2.14.

Consider discretely self-similar data as in Definition 2.1. Then, for $0<\kappa\ll 1$ sufficiently small and for $v\in[0,\infty)$ , we have that

$$ \big|\partial_{u}\phi(-1,v)-\partial_{u}\phi(p)\big|\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa}\frac{v}{v+1}. $$

#### Proof.

We can rewrite the wave equation (1.7) as $\partial_{v}(r\partial_{u}\phi)=-\partial_{v}\phi\partial_{u}r.$ Thus, on $u=-1$ we have:

$$ r\partial_{u}\phi(-1,v)-r\partial_{u}\phi(p)=O\bigg(\sqrt{\kappa}\frac{v}{v+1}\bigg). $$

We can rewrite this as

$$ r(-1,v)\cdot\big(\partial_{u}\phi(-1,v)-\partial_{u}\phi(p)\big)=-\big(r(-1,v)-1\big)\cdot\partial_{u}\phi(p)+O\big(\sqrt{\kappa}v\big)=O\big(\sqrt{\kappa}v\big), $$

where we also used (2.6) and (2.33). ∎

### 2.4 Proof of Proposition 2.4

#### Proof of Proposition 2.4.

Let $\Delta>0$ and $\kappa>0$ be arbitrary. For the seed data along $C_{0}^{-}$ we make the ansatz $\phi=\sqrt{\kappa}\alpha\psi$ for a fixed $\psi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(-1,e^{-\Delta}),\psi\not\equiv 0$ which we continue self-similarly according to (2.3). This ensures (2.6). By modulating $\alpha$ as a function of $\Delta$ and $\psi$ , we can verify (2.5) by the intermediate value theorem. Thus there exists a constant $C_{data}>0$ only depending on $\Delta$ (and the fixed profile $\psi$ ) satisfying (2.6).

In order to ensure that $\mu$ is self-similar, it suffices to show that $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r$ is self-similar. We specify $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r$ at $p$ according to (2.17). Indeed, using (2.11), we compute

$$ \displaystyle\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r \displaystyle(e^{-\Delta}u,0)=\frac{e^{F(u)}}{-u}e^{\Delta+\kappa\Delta}\left(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)-\frac{1}{4}\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}-\frac{1}{4}\int_{-e^{-\Delta}}^{e^{-\Delta}u}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\right) \displaystyle=\frac{e^{F(u)}}{-u}e^{\Delta+\kappa\Delta}\left(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)+\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(p)(e^{\Delta(-\kappa-1)}-1)-\frac{e^{-(1+\kappa)\Delta}}{4}\int_{-1}^{u}e^{-F(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\right) \displaystyle=\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0) $$

which shows (2.7).

To show (2.8), we specify $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)$ at $p$ according to (2.25). Then, using (2.26) we compute

$$ \displaystyle\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi) \displaystyle(e^{-\Delta}u,0)=e^{F(u)}e^{\kappa\Delta}\left(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)-\int_{-1}^{-e^{-\Delta}}\frac{e^{-F(u^{\prime})}}{-4u^{\prime}}\mu\phi du^{\prime}-\int_{-e^{-\Delta}}^{e^{-\Delta}u}\frac{e^{-F(u^{\prime})}}{-4u^{\prime}}\mu\phi du^{\prime}\right) \displaystyle=e^{F(u)}e^{\kappa\Delta}\left(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)+\frac{1-e^{\kappa\Delta}}{e^{\kappa\Delta}}\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)-e^{-\kappa\Delta}\int_{-1}^{u}\frac{e^{-F(u^{\prime})}}{-4u^{\prime}}\mu\phi du^{\prime}\right) \displaystyle=\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(u,0) $$

which shows (2.8). Since $|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}(r\phi)(p)|\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa}$ , by potentially making $C_{data}$ larger depending only on $\Delta$ and the choice of $\psi$ , we readily find data $\phi=\sqrt{\kappa}\tilde{\psi}$ on $C_{0}^{+}$ satisfying (2.8). The condition (2.9) follows now from (2.8) and the discrete self-similarity of $\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r$ shown above. Note that the gauge $\Omega^{2}=\frac{1}{1-\kappa}$ in $C_{0}^{+}$ uniquely determines $r$ on $C_{0}^{+}$ . ∎

## 3 Construction of the exterior region $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}$

In this section we will prove our main result Theorem 1. Throughout Section 3 we fix the parameter $\Delta>0$ . We also introduce an additional parameter

$$ 0<\delta\ll 1 $$

which is small and independent of all other parameters. For instance, setting $\delta=10^{-5}$ would work for our proof. We consider discretely self-similar characteristic data with period $\Delta$ for ( $r,\Omega^{2},\phi$ ) on $C_{0}^{-}\cup_{p}C_{0}^{+}$ as defined in Definition 2.1. According to Proposition 2.4, there exists a $C_{data}(\Delta)>0$ such that for all $\kappa>0$ , and $N\geq 1$ , there exists such nontrivial discretely self-similar characteristic data with period $\Delta$ . For the rest of Section 3 we fix the parameters

$$ \delta,\Delta,C_{data}(\Delta),\text{ and }N $$

and we will use the following convention. For non-negative quantities $A$ and $B$ , we write $A\lesssim B$ (or also $A=O(B)$ ) if there exists a constant $\tilde{C}>0$ only depending on $\delta$ , $\Delta$ , and $C_{data}(\Delta)$ such that $A\leq\tilde{C}B$ . We will also write “for sufficiently small $A>0$ ” if there exists a constant $A_{0}>0$ sufficiently small and only depending on $\delta$ , $\Delta$ , and $C_{data}(\Delta)$ such that $A$ satisfies $0<A\leq A_{0}$ . Similarly, we write “for sufficiently small $A>0$ depending on $B$ ” if there exists a constant $A_{0}>0$ sufficiently small and only depending on $\delta$ , $\Delta$ , $C_{data}(\Delta)$ and $B$ such that $A$ satisfies $0<A\leq A_{0}$ .

#### Hierarchy of scales

In the proofs in Section 3 we will introduce further parameters of different scales. Our hierarchy of scales is

$$ \kappa(\delta,\underline{v},D)\ll\frac{1}{D(\delta,\underline{v})}\ll\underline{v}(\delta)\ll\delta\ll 1, $$

where we suppressed the additional dependence on the parameters $\Delta,C_{data},k$ occurring in (3.2). We will also make use of $\epsilon\doteq 40\delta$ and $\eta\doteq 10\epsilon=400\delta$ .

By standard local existence results (see e.g. [Daf05, Proposition 1.1]), data as in Definition 2.1 give rise to a unique solution

$$ (r,\Omega^{2},\phi)\in C^{N+2}(\mathcal{R}_{0})\times C^{N+1}(\mathcal{R}_{0})\times C^{N+1}(\mathcal{R}_{0}) $$

in the domain

$$ \mathcal{R}_{0}=\big\{(u,v)\in\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}:v\in[0,v_{*}(u)]\big\} $$

for some function $v_{*}(u)>0$ . A priori, however, we have no control on the size of this domain as $u\rightarrow 0$ .

#### The decomposition of $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}$ into the regions $\mathcal{R}_{I}$ – $\mathcal{R}_{IV}$

In order to show Theorem 1 we have to show that $(r,\Omega^{2},\phi)$ extends to the whole domain $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}$ . Of course, the difficulty is to show existence as uniqueness follows readily. To show existence in $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}$ we will split up the region $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}$ into four regions $\mathcal{R}_{I}$ – $\mathcal{R}_{IV}$ and treat each region independently, see Fig. 4. This decomposition was first established in [RS23] and also used in [Sin24]. We begin with region $\mathcal{R}_{I}$ .

### 3.1 Region $\mathcal{R}_{I}$

We define

$$ \mathcal{R}_{I}\doteq\bigg\{(u,v)\in\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}:v\in[0,\underline{v}^{1-\kappa}],\ \frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}}\leq\underline{v}^{1-\kappa}\bigg\}, $$

which depends on a small parameter $\underline{v}>0$ .

#### Proposition 3.1.

For $\underline{v}>0$ sufficiently small and $\kappa>0$ sufficiently small depending on $\underline{v}$ , the solution $(r,\Omega^{2},\phi)$ of (3.4) exists in region $\mathcal{R}_{I}$ . Moreover, $(r,\Omega^{2},\phi)$ satisfies the estimates (3.10)–(3.14) in region $\mathcal{R}_{I}$ .

We will prove Proposition 3.1 as a consequence of Proposition 3.2 below at the end of Section 3.1.

#### Bootstrap Assumptions

Our proof will be based on a bootstrap argument and we will now formulate the bootstrap assumptions.

We consider the following bootstrap assumptions

$$ \displaystyle\big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi(u,v)-\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi(u,0)\big| \displaystyle\leq 100C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1}\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-2\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-2\delta}} \displaystyle\big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,v)-\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)\big| \displaystyle\leq 100C\cdot\kappa\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}\phi(u,v)-\partial_{u}\phi(u,0)\big| \displaystyle\leq 100C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1}\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}r(u,v)-\partial_{u}r(u,0)\big| \displaystyle\leq 100C\cdot\kappa\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} \displaystyle\bigg|\log\frac{1-\kappa}{|u|^{\kappa}}\Omega^{2}-\log\Big(|u|^{-\kappa}e^{-F(u)}\Big)\bigg| \displaystyle\leq 100C\cdot\kappa\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} $$

for some constant $C>0$ depending only on the fixed parameters in (3.2). In particular, in view of our convention, we have $C\lesssim 1$ .

#### Proposition 3.2.

For any $(u_{1},v_{1})\in\mathcal{R}_{I},$ we assume that the bootstrap assumptions (3.5)–(3.9) hold for all $(u,v)\in\mathcal{R}^{I}_{u_{1},v_{1}}=[-1,u_{1}]\times[0,v_{1}].$ Then, the following improved estimates hold in $\mathcal{R}^{I}_{u_{1},v_{1}}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi(u,v)-\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi(u,0)\big| \displaystyle\leq 10C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1}\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-2\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-2\delta}} \displaystyle\big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,v)-\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)\big| \displaystyle\leq 10C\cdot\kappa\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}\phi(u,v)-\partial_{u}\phi(u,0)\big| \displaystyle\leq 10C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1}\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}r(u,v)-\partial_{u}r(u,0)\big| \displaystyle\leq 10C\cdot\kappa\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} \displaystyle\bigg|\log\frac{1-\kappa}{|u|^{\kappa}}\Omega^{2}-\log\Big(|u|^{-\kappa}e^{-F(u)}\Big)\bigg| \displaystyle\leq 10C\cdot\kappa\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} $$

#### Proof of Proposition 3.2.

The bootstrap assumptions hold initially by continuity: We first notice that the left hand sides vanish on the incoming cone $v=0.$ Similarly, by choosing $C$ sufficiently large, the bootstrap assumptions hold on $u=-1$ with $C$ instead of $100C,$ because of the choice of initial data and the previous estimates on the outgoing cone $\{u=-1\}.$ For the rest of the proof of Proposition 3.2, we will assume that the bootstrap assumptions hold in $\mathcal{R}^{I}_{u_{1},v_{1}}$ and we prove the desired improved estimates.

#### Preliminary Estimates

As a consequence of the bootstrap assumptions and the estimates on the initial data and by choosing $\underline{v}>0$ sufficiently small, we get the bounds:

$$ \big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi(u,v)\big|\leq 2C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1} $$

$$ 0<\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,v)\leq 1,\ \big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,v)-\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)\big|\leq\kappa $$

$$ \big|\partial_{u}\phi(u,v)\big|\leq 2C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1} $$

$$ \big|\partial_{u}r(u,v)\big|\leq 2,\ \big|\partial_{u}r(u,v)-\partial_{u}r(u,0)\big|\leq\kappa $$

$$ 1-2C\kappa\leq\frac{1-\kappa}{|u|^{\kappa}}\Omega^{2}\leq 1+2C\kappa $$

We also have the estimates for $r$ :

#### Lemma 3.3.

The area radius $r$ satisfies the following bounds:

$$ 0\leq r(u,v)+u\leq 4Cv|u|^{\kappa}\leq|u| $$

$$ |r^{-1}(u,v)+u^{-1}|\leq 4C\cdot\frac{1}{|u|}\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}} $$

$$ r(u,v)=-u\cdot\bigg(1+\frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{1}{1-\kappa}\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}}+O\bigg(\kappa\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}}\bigg)\bigg) $$

#### Proof.

Since $\partial_{v}r>0$ and $r=-u$ on $C_{0}^{-}$ we have that $-u\leq r(u,v)$ in $\mathcal{R}_{I}$ Moreover, we have

$$ r(u,v)+u\leq\int_{0}^{v}\Omega^{2}\cdot\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq 4Cv|u|^{\kappa}\leq|u| $$

for $\underline{v}$ sufficiently small. Moreover,

$$ |r^{-1}(u,v)+u^{-1}|\leq\frac{|r(u,v)+u|}{u^{2}}\leq 4C\cdot\frac{1}{|u|}\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}} $$

as well as

$$ r(u,v)=-u+\int_{0}^{v}\Omega^{2}\cdot\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}=-u+\int_{0}^{v}\frac{|u|^{\kappa}}{1-\kappa}\cdot\big(1+O(\kappa)\big)\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{4}+O(\kappa)\bigg)dv^{\prime} $$

which concludes the proof of Lemma 3.3. ∎

#### Main Estimates

We will now improve the bootstrap assumptions, completing the proof of Proposition 3.2. We introduce the following notation: for any function $\psi$ we define:

$$ \widetilde{\psi}(u,v):=\psi(u,v)-\psi(u,0) $$

We begin by improving assumption (3.9). Notice that we have the equation:

$$ \partial_{u}\partial_{v}\log\frac{1-\kappa}{|u|^{\kappa}}\Omega^{2}=-2\partial_{u}\phi\partial_{v}\phi+\frac{\Omega^{2}}{2r^{2}}+\frac{2\partial_{v}r\partial_{u}r}{r^{2}}=-2\partial_{u}\phi\partial_{v}\phi+\frac{\Omega^{2}}{2r^{2}}\bigg(1+4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r\partial_{u}r\bigg)= $$

$$ =-2\partial_{u}\phi\partial_{v}\phi+\frac{\Omega^{2}}{2r^{2}}\bigg(4\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r}\cdot\partial_{u}r+4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)\cdot\widetilde{\partial_{u}r}+1-4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)\bigg) $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions and the preliminary estimates, we have

$$ \partial_{u}\partial_{v}\log\frac{1-\kappa}{|u|^{\kappa}}\Omega^{2}=O\big(\kappa\cdot|u|^{-2+\kappa}\big) $$

We integrate from $-1$ to $u,$ and use the fact that $(1-\kappa)\Omega^{2}(-1,v)=1$ , in order to obtain that:

$$ \bigg|\partial_{v}\log\frac{1-\kappa}{|u|^{\kappa}}\Omega^{2}\bigg|=O\big(\kappa\cdot|u|^{-1+\kappa}\big) $$

We integrate from $0$ to $v$ and obtain.

$$ \bigg|\log\frac{1-\kappa}{|u|^{\kappa}}\Omega^{2}-\log\Big(|u|^{-\kappa}e^{-F(u)}\Big)\bigg|\lesssim\kappa\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}}\lesssim\kappa\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}}\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{\delta}}\leq\kappa\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}}\cdot\underline{v}^{\delta}. $$

By choosing $\underline{v}$ sufficiently small we improve the constant in (3.9). Thus, we proved (3.14).

We improve assumption (3.6) next. We have by equation (1.9), together with the bootstrap assumptions and the preliminary estimates:

$$ \big|\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r}\big|\leq\int_{0}^{v}r\cdot\Omega^{2}\cdot\big(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi\big)^{2}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\lesssim\int_{0}^{v}\kappa\cdot|u|^{\kappa-1}dv^{\prime}\lesssim\kappa\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}}, $$

which improves assumption (3.6) as before. Thus, we proved (3.11).

We improve assumption (3.7). From the wave equation (1.7), the bootstrap assumptions, and the preliminary estimates we have that

$$ \big|\widetilde{r\partial_{u}\phi}\big|(u,v)\leq\int_{0}^{v}\big|\partial_{u}r\big|\cdot\Omega^{2}\cdot\big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi\big|dv^{\prime}\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}}. $$

Moreover, we also have the estimate:

$$ r(u,v)\cdot\big|\widetilde{\partial_{u}\phi}\big|\leq\big|\widetilde{r\partial_{u}\phi}\big|(u,v)+\big|\widetilde{r}\big|(u,v)\cdot\big|\partial_{u}\phi\big|(u,0)\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}}, $$

where we used the previous bound for $\widetilde{r\partial_{u}\phi},$ the bound on initial data for $\partial_{u}\phi(u,0)$ , and the preliminary bound for $\widetilde{r}(u,v).$ This improves assumption (3.7) as before, so we obtain (3.12).

We improve assumption (3.8). Note that we can write equation (1.6) as:

$$ \partial_{v}\big(r\cdot\widetilde{\partial_{u}r}\big)=-\frac{\Omega^{2}}{4}+\partial_{v}r=\Omega^{2}\cdot\bigg(\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r}(u,v)+\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)-\frac{1}{4}\bigg)=O\big(\kappa\cdot|u|^{\kappa}\big) $$

We integrate this and divide by $r(u,v)$ in order to get:

$$ \widetilde{\partial_{u}r}=O\bigg(\kappa\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1-\kappa}}\bigg) $$

Finally, we improve assumption (3.5). We use (1.7) in order to obtain a suitable equation for $\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi}.$ We write (1.7) as

$$ \partial_{u}\big(\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi\big)=-\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi\cdot\bigg(\frac{\partial_{u}r}{r}-\partial_{u}\log\Omega^{-2}\bigg)-\frac{1}{r}\partial_{u}\phi\cdot\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r $$

from which we derive the following equation for $\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi}$ :

$$ \partial_{u}\left(\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi}\right)+\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi}\cdot\big(\partial_{u}\log r(u,0)-F^{\prime}(u)\big)\\
=-\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{r}\cdot\widetilde{\partial_{u}r}-\widetilde{r^{-1}}-\widetilde{\partial_{u}\log\Omega^{-2}}\bigg)-\frac{1}{r}\cdot\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r\cdot\widetilde{\partial_{u}\phi}\\
-\partial_{u}\phi(u,0)\cdot\frac{1}{r}\cdot\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r}-\partial_{u}\phi(u,0)\cdot\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r(u,0)\cdot\widetilde{r^{-1}} $$

Using (3.20) we estimate

$$ |\widetilde{\partial_{u}\log\Omega^{-2}}|\lesssim\kappa|u|^{-2+\kappa}v $$

which together with the bootstrap assumptions and the preliminary estimates, gives us

$$ \partial_{u}\left(\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi}\right)+\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi}\cdot\big(\partial_{u}\log r(u,0)-F^{\prime}(u)\big)=O\bigg(\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-2}\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}}\bigg) $$

We integrate this equation to obtain:

$$ \displaystyle|\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi}|(u,v) \displaystyle\lesssim\frac{e^{F(u)}}{|u|}\cdot|\widetilde{\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi}|(-1,v)+\frac{e^{F(u)}}{|u|}\cdot\int_{-1}^{u}\frac{|u^{\prime}|}{e^{F(u^{\prime})}}\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u^{\prime}|^{-2}\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u^{\prime}|^{1-\kappa-\delta}}du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1+\kappa}}+\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}}{|u|^{1+\kappa}}\cdot\int_{-1}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-1+\kappa}\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u^{\prime}|^{1-\kappa-\delta}}du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot\frac{v}{|u|^{1+\kappa}}+\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1}\cdot\frac{v^{\frac{1-\kappa-\delta}{1-\kappa}}}{|u|^{1-\kappa-\delta}} $$

where we used the initial data estimates (2.10) and (2.12). Since $1\leq|u|^{-1}$ and $\underline{v}^{\delta}\ll 1,$ we proved (3.10). This completes the proof of Proposition 3.2. ∎

#### Proof of Proposition 3.1.

Proposition 3.2 implies Proposition 3.1 by a standard local existence argument. ∎

In particular, the solution $(r,\Omega^{2},\phi)$ exists on the spacelike hypersurface $\big\{v=\underline{v}^{1-\kappa}|u|^{1-\kappa}\big\},$ and satisfies the following smallness result:

#### Corollary 3.1.

The solution $(r,\Omega^{2},\phi)$ satisfies the following estimates on the spacelike hypersurface $\big\{v=\underline{v}^{1-\kappa}|u|^{1-\kappa}\big\}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\big|\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq 2C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1} \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq 2C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1} \displaystyle\big|4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{v}r-1\big| \displaystyle\leq 2C\cdot\kappa, \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}r+1\big| \displaystyle\leq 2C\cdot\kappa, \displaystyle\big||u|^{-\kappa}\Omega^{2}-1\big| \displaystyle\leq 2C\cdot\kappa \displaystyle r \displaystyle=-u\cdot\left(1+\frac{1}{4}\cdot\underline{v}+O(\kappa^{1-\delta})\right) $$

for some constant $C>0$ with $C\lesssim 1$ .

### 3.2 Region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$

In this section we prove the existence of the solution in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ . As explained in the introduction, we consider a new system of double null coordinates $(u,V)$ , with respect to which the solution is close to Minkowski space in standard null coordinates. We define on $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}\setminus\mathcal{R}_{I}$ the new coordinates

$$ V(u,v)=v^{\frac{1}{1-\kappa}},\quad u(u,v)=u, $$

in mild abuse of notation. We remark that the associated transition map is a smooth diffeomorphism on $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}\setminus\mathcal{R}_{I}$ and the metric is given by

$$ g=-\bar{\Omega}^{2}(u,V)dudV+r^{2}d\sigma_{S^{2}}, $$

where the new lapse function $\bar{\Omega}^{2}$ is given as

$$ \bar{\Omega}^{2}(u,V)=(1-\kappa)\cdot V^{-\kappa}\cdot\Omega^{2}(u,v(V)). $$

We define

$$ \mathcal{R}_{II}=\bigg\{(u,V):\ u\in[-1,0),\ V\in[0,\underline{v}^{-1}],\ \underline{v}\leq\frac{V}{|u|}\leq\underline{v}^{-1}\bigg\} $$

and the main result of this section is

#### Proposition 3.4.

For $\underline{v}>0$ sufficiently small and $\kappa>0$ sufficiently small depending on $\underline{v}$ , the solution $(r,\Omega^{2},\phi)$ exists in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ . Moreover, the solution satisfies the estimates (3.28)–(3.32) in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ .

The proof follows the ideas of [RS23], by proving estimates which correspond to applying the Gronwall lemma starting from data at $\big\{V=\underline{v}|u|\big\}\cup\big\{u=-1,\ V\in[\underline{v},\underline{v}^{-1}]\big\}.$

#### Bootstrap Assumptions

We introduce a large constant $D\gg 1$ which depends on $\underline{v}$ (and on the parameters in (3.2)). We will choose $\kappa$ sufficiently small depending on $D,\underline{v}$ (and on the parameters in (3.2)) such that

$$ \kappa^{\delta}\cdot\exp\bigg(\bigg(\frac{D}{\underline{v}}\bigg)^{100}\bigg)\ll 1. $$

We make the following bootstrap assumptions in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\bigg|\frac{V}{4}-u\bigg|\cdot|\partial_{V}\phi|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta} \displaystyle\bigg|\frac{V}{4}-u\bigg|\cdot|\partial_{u}\phi|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta} \displaystyle\bigg|\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{1-10\delta} \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}r+1\big|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{1-10\delta} \displaystyle\big|\bar{\Omega}^{2}-1\big|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{1-8\delta} $$

The local existence result implies that Proposition 3.4 follows once we prove

#### Proposition 3.5.

For any $(u_{1},V_{1})\in\mathcal{R}_{II},$ we assume that the solution satisfies the bootstrap assumptions (3.23)–(3.27) for all $(u,V)\in\mathcal{R}^{II}_{u_{1},V_{1}}=\mathcal{R}_{II}\cap\big([-1,u_{1}]\times[0,V_{1}]\big).$ Then the solution satisfies the improved estimates in $\mathcal{R}^{II}_{u_{1},V_{1}}:$

$$ \displaystyle\bigg|\frac{V}{4}-u\bigg|\cdot|\partial_{V}\phi|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta} \displaystyle\bigg|\frac{V}{4}-u\bigg|\cdot|\partial_{u}\phi|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta} \displaystyle\bigg|\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{1-10\delta} \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}r+1\big|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{1-10\delta} \displaystyle\big|\bar{\Omega}^{2}-1\big|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg) \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{1-8\delta} $$

We notice that the bootstrap assumptions hold initially on $\big\{V=\underline{v}|u|\big\}$ since we can rewrite the estimates in Corollary 3.1 in $(u,V)$ coordinates as:

$$ \big|\partial_{V}\phi\big|(u,-\underline{v}u)\leq 4C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1},\ \big|\partial_{u}\phi\big|(u,-\underline{v}u)\leq 2C\cdot\sqrt{\kappa}\cdot|u|^{-1} $$

$$ \big|4\partial_{V}r(u,-\underline{v}u)-1\big|\leq\kappa^{1-2\delta},\ \big|\partial_{u}r(u,-\underline{v}u)+1\big|\leq 2C\cdot\kappa $$

$$ 1-C\kappa^{1-\delta}\leq\bar{\Omega}^{2}(u,-\underline{v}u)\leq 1+C\kappa^{1-\delta} $$

Similarly, the bootstrap assumptions hold initially on $\big\{u=-1,\ V\in[\underline{v},\underline{v}^{-1}]\big\},$ since we can rewrite the estimates on the outgoing initial data in $(u,V)$ coordinates as:

$$ \big|\partial_{V}\phi\big|(-1,V)\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\delta}{2}}\cdot V^{-1},\ \big|\partial_{u}\phi\big|(-1,V)\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\delta}{2}}\cdot V^{-1} $$

$$ \big|4\partial_{V}r(-1,V)-1\big|\leq\kappa^{1-2\delta},\ \big|\partial_{u}r(-1,V)+1\big|\leq\kappa^{1-2\delta} $$

$$ 1-\kappa^{1-\delta}\leq\bar{\Omega}^{2}(-1,V)\leq 1+\kappa^{1-\delta} $$

For the rest of the section we prove Proposition 3.5, so we assume that the bootstrap assumptions hold in $\mathcal{R}^{II}_{u_{1},V_{1}}$ and we prove the desired improved estimates.

#### Preliminary Estimates

As a consequence of the bootstrap assumptions, we have the following simple bounds

$$ \displaystyle|\partial_{u}\phi| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-2\delta}|u|^{-1},\quad|\partial_{V}\phi|\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-2\delta}|u|^{-1} \displaystyle\frac{1}{8} \displaystyle\leq|\partial_{V}r|\leq\frac{1}{2}\leq|\partial_{u}r|,\quad|\bar{\Omega}^{2}|\leq 2. $$

We also have the following estimate for $r:$

#### Lemma 3.6.

The area radius function $r$ satisfies:

$$ r(u,V)=\frac{V}{4}-u+O(|u|\kappa^{1-11\delta}) $$

#### Proof.

Using the bootstrap assumptions and Corollary 3.1, we have

$$ r(u,V)=r(u,-\underline{v}u)+\int_{-\underline{v}u}^{V}\partial_{V}r(u,V^{\prime})dV^{\prime}=\frac{V}{4}-u+O(|u|\kappa^{1-\delta})+O\bigg(\underline{v}^{-1}\cdot\exp\bigg(\frac{D}{\underline{v}}\bigg)\cdot|u|\kappa^{1-10\delta}\bigg) $$

which leads to the desired conclusion by (3.22). ∎

#### Main Estimates

We improve the bootstrap assumptions, completing the proof of Proposition 3.5. We begin by improving assumption (3.23). We can rewrite the wave equation (1.7) as:

$$ \partial_{u}\bigg(\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{V}\phi\bigg)=-D\cdot\frac{V}{u^{2}}\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{V}\phi-\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\partial_{V}r\partial_{u}\phi $$

We multiply the equation in order to obtain:

$$ \partial_{u}\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{V}\phi\bigg|^{2}+2D\cdot\frac{V}{u^{2}}\cdot\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{V}\phi\bigg|^{2}=-2\exp\bigg(2D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\partial_{V}r\partial_{u}\phi\cdot r\partial_{V}\phi $$

We denote $b(V)=\max\big\{-1,-V/\underline{v}\big\}.$ We integrate the above equation and absorb an error term to obtain the energy estimate

$$ \displaystyle\bigg|\exp\bigg(D \displaystyle\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{V}\phi\bigg|^{2}(u,V)+D\int_{b(V)}^{u}\frac{V}{u^{\prime 2}}\cdot\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u^{\prime}}\bigg)r\partial_{V}\phi\bigg|^{2}(u^{\prime},V)du^{\prime} \displaystyle\leq\big|\exp\big(-D\underline{v}\big)r\partial_{V}\phi\big|^{2}(b(V),V)+D^{-1}\int_{b(V)}^{u}\frac{u^{\prime 2}}{V}\cdot\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u^{\prime}}\bigg)\partial_{V}r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg|^{2}(u^{\prime},V)du^{\prime}. $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions, the preliminary estimates, and the bounds of the solution on $\big\{V=-\underline{v}u\big\}$ and $\big\{u=-1,\ V\in[\underline{v},\underline{v}^{-1}]\big\}$ , we get

$$ \bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{V}\phi\bigg|^{2}(u,V)\leq\kappa^{1-2\delta}+D^{-1}\cdot\kappa^{1-2\delta}\cdot O(\underline{v}^{-1}). $$

Using the preliminary estimates for $r$ , we obtain that

$$ \bigg|\frac{V}{4}-u\bigg|\cdot|\partial_{V}\phi|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)(u,V)\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta}\cdot\bigg(1+D^{-\frac{1}{2}}\cdot O(\underline{v}^{-\frac{1}{2}})+O(\kappa^{1-12\delta})\bigg) $$

which improves the bootstrap assumption (3.23) for $D$ large enough. Thus, we proved (3.28).

Similarly, we improve assumption (3.24). We can rewrite the wave equation (1.7) as

$$ \partial_{V}\bigg(\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg)=D\cdot\frac{1}{u}\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{u}\phi-\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\partial_{u}r\partial_{V}\phi $$

We multiply the equation in order to obtain:

$$ \partial_{V}\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg|^{2}+2D\cdot\frac{1}{|u|}\cdot\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg|^{2}=-2\exp\bigg(2D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\partial_{u}r\partial_{V}\phi\cdot r\partial_{u}\phi $$

We integrate this equation and absorb an error term to obtain the energy estimate:

$$ \bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg|^{2}(u,V)+D\int_{-\underline{v}u}^{V}\frac{1}{|u|}\cdot\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V^{\prime}}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg|^{2}(u,V^{\prime})dV^{\prime}\leq $$

$$ \leq\big|\exp\big(-D\underline{v}\big)r\partial_{u}\phi\big|^{2}(u,-\underline{v}u)+D^{-1}\int_{-\underline{v}u}^{V}|u|\cdot\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V^{\prime}}{u}\bigg)\partial_{u}r\partial_{V}\phi\bigg|^{2}(u,V^{\prime})dV^{\prime} $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions, the preliminary estimates, and the bounds of the solution on $\{V=-\underline{v}u\}$ , we get that for some constant $C^{\prime}>0$ independent of $\kappa,D,\underline{v},$ and $\delta$ :

$$ \bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg|^{2}(u,V)\leq C^{\prime}\kappa+D^{-1}\cdot\kappa^{1-2\delta}\cdot O(\underline{v}^{-1}) $$

Using the preliminary estimates for $r$ , we obtain that:

$$ \bigg|\frac{V}{4}-u\bigg|\cdot|\partial_{u}\phi|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)(u,V)\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta}\cdot\bigg(1+D^{-\frac{1}{2}}\cdot O(\underline{v}^{-\frac{1}{2}})+O(\kappa^{1-12\delta})\bigg), $$

which improves the bootstrap assumption (3.24) and proves (3.29).

Next, we improve assumption (3.25). We can rewrite the Raychaudhuri equation (1.9) as:

$$ \partial_{V}\bigg(\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg)=-r\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\big(\partial_{V}\phi\big)^{2} $$

We integrate this equation to obtain:

$$ \bigg|\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg|(u,V)\leq\bigg|\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg|(u,-\underline{v}u)+\int_{-\underline{v}u}^{V}r\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\big(\partial_{V}\phi\big)^{2}(u,V^{\prime})dV^{\prime} $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions, the preliminary estimates, and the bounds of the solution on $\{V=-\underline{v}u\}$ , we get:

$$ \bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\cdot\bigg(\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg)\bigg|(u,V)\leq\kappa^{1-3\delta}+\kappa^{1-2\delta}\cdot\exp\bigg(3\frac{D}{\underline{v}}\bigg)\cdot O(\underline{v}^{-1})\leq\kappa^{1-4\delta} $$

As a result, we obtain that:

$$ \bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\cdot\bigg(\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg)\bigg|\leq\bigg|\bar{\Omega}^{2}\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\cdot\bigg(\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg)\bigg|+\frac{1}{4}\bigg|\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\cdot\big(\bar{\Omega}^{2}-1\big)\bigg|\leq 2\kappa^{1-10\delta} $$

We point out that since we use the bootstrap assumption (3.27) in the above inequality, the assumption (3.25) must have a lower power of $\kappa$ than (3.27). Also, we remark that a completely analogous proof improves assumption (3.26). Thus, we proved (3.30) and (3.31).

Finally, we improve assumption (3.27). The key point is that we avoid using the estimates (3.25) and (3.26) (which do not have small enough powers of $\kappa$ for our purposes) by using the Hawking mass instead. We use that $\bar{\Omega}^{-2}(-\partial_{u}r)=\frac{1-\mu}{4\partial_{V}r}$ and substitute it in (1.10) to obtain

$$ \partial_{V}m=\big(2\partial_{V}r\big)^{-1}\cdot\bigg(1-\frac{2m}{r}\bigg)\cdot r^{2}(\partial_{V}\phi)^{2}. $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions and the preliminary estimates, we get that $|\partial_{V}m|\leq\kappa^{1-3\delta}.$ Also, by the bounds on the hypersurface $\{V=-\underline{v}u\},$ we have $\frac{m}{r}(u,-\underline{v}u)=O(\kappa).$ Therefore, we have that in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ :

$$ \frac{m}{r}\leq\kappa^{1-4\delta} $$

The relation between (3.27) and the Hawking mass follows from the equation

$$ \partial_{u}\partial_{V}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}=-2\partial_{u}\phi\partial_{V}\phi+\frac{\bar{\Omega}^{2}}{r^{2}}\cdot\frac{m}{r}. $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions and the bound for the Hawking mass, we obtain that:

$$ \big|\partial_{u}\partial_{V}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big|\leq|u|^{-2}\kappa^{1-5\delta} $$

We claim that the analysis in region $\mathcal{R}_{I}$ implies that $\partial_{u}\log\Omega^{2}\big(u,|\underline{v}u|^{1-\kappa}\big)=O(\kappa|u|^{-1}).$ Indeed, we already proved that $\widetilde{\partial_{u}\log\Omega^{2}}=O(\kappa|u|^{-1})$ and $\partial_{u}\log\Omega^{2}(u,0)=O(\kappa|u|^{-1}).$ Moreover, we notice that we also have $\partial_{u}\log\Omega^{2}\big(u,|\underline{v}u|^{1-\kappa}\big)=\partial_{u}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}(u,-\underline{v}u).$ Thus, we integrate the above in the $V$ direction in order to get:

$$ \big|\partial_{u}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big|\leq V^{-1}\kappa^{1-6\delta}. $$

Finally, we integrate this in the $u$ direction and use the bounds on $\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}$ on the hypersurfaces $\big\{V=-\underline{v}u\big\}$ and $\big\{u=-1,\ V\in[\underline{v},\underline{v}^{-1}]\big\}$ to get:

$$ \big|\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big|\leq\kappa^{1-7\delta} $$

This implies that

$$ \big|\bar{\Omega}^{2}-1\big|\cdot\exp\bigg(D\cdot\frac{V}{u}\bigg)\leq\kappa^{1-8\delta} $$

improving assumption (3.27) and proving (3.32). This completes the proof of Proposition 3.5.∎

As before, Proposition 3.5 implies Proposition 3.4, giving existence of the solution in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ . Moreover, in the $(u,V)$ coordinates, the solution is close to Minkowski space in standard null coordinates. In particular, on the spacelike hypersurface $\big\{u=-\underline{v}V\big\}$ we have the following smallness result:

#### Corollary 3.2.

We denote $\epsilon=40\delta.$ The solution constructed in Proposition 3.4 satisfies the following estimates on the spacelike hypersurface $\big\{u=-\underline{v}V\big\}$ :

$$ \big|\partial_{V}\phi\big|\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\epsilon}{2}}\cdot V^{-1},\ \big|\partial_{u}\phi\big|\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\epsilon}{2}}\cdot V^{-1} $$

$$ \big|4\partial_{V}r-1\big|\leq\kappa^{1-\frac{\epsilon}{2}},\ \big|\partial_{u}r+1\big|\leq\kappa^{1-\frac{\epsilon}{2}},\ \big|\bar{\Omega}^{2}-1\big|\leq\kappa^{1-\frac{\epsilon}{2}} $$

$$ r=\frac{V}{4}-u+O(V\cdot\kappa^{1-\frac{\epsilon}{2}}) $$

### 3.3 Region $\mathcal{R}_{III}$

In this section we prove the existence of the solution in region $\mathcal{R}_{III}$ . Once again, it is convenient to work in the double null coordinates $(u,V)$ . The main result of this section is

#### Proposition 3.7.

Let $(M,g,\phi)$ be the solution of (1.1) constructed in Proposition 3.4. For $\kappa,\underline{v}>0$ sufficiently small, the solution exists in region $\mathcal{R}_{III}$ :

$$ \mathcal{R}_{III}=\bigg\{(u,V):\ u\in[-1,0),\ V\in(0,1],\ \frac{V}{|u|}\geq\underline{v}^{-1}\bigg\}. $$

Moreover, the solution satisfies the estimates (3.42)–(3.46) in region $\mathcal{R}_{III}$ .

#### Bootstrap Assumptions

Let $p>0$ be a small constant (for example $p=1/10$ is sufficient). We consider the following bootstrap assumptions:

$$ \displaystyle V\cdot\big|\partial_{V}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon} \displaystyle V\cdot\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}\cdot\big|\partial_{u}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon} \displaystyle\bigg|\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg| \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{1-2\epsilon} \displaystyle\big|\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{u}r+1\big| \displaystyle\leq 100\kappa^{1-2\epsilon} \displaystyle\big|\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big| \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\cdot\bigg(1+100\log\bigg|\frac{V\underline{v}}{u}\bigg|\bigg) $$

A standard local existence argument implies that Proposition 3.7 follows if we prove the following result:

#### Proposition 3.8.

For any $(u_{1},V_{1})\in\mathcal{R}_{III},$ we assume that the solution satisfies the bootstrap assumptions (3.37)–(3.41) for all $(u,V)\in\mathcal{R}^{III}_{u_{1},V_{1}}=\mathcal{R}_{III}\cap\big([-1,u_{1}]\times[0,V_{1}]\big).$ Then the solution satisfies the improved estimates in $\mathcal{R}^{III}_{u_{1},V_{1}}$ :

$$ \displaystyle V\cdot\big|\partial_{V}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon} \displaystyle V\cdot\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}\cdot\big|\partial_{u}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon} \displaystyle\bigg|\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg| \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{1-2\epsilon} \displaystyle\big|\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{u}r+1\big| \displaystyle\leq 10\kappa^{1-2\epsilon} \displaystyle\big|\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\cdot\bigg(1+10\log\bigg|\frac{V\underline{v}}{u}\bigg|\bigg). $$

#### Proof of Proposition 3.8.

We notice that the bootstrap assumptions hold initially on the spacelike hypersurface $\big\{u=-\underline{v}V\big\}$ because of Corollary 3.2. For the rest of the section, we assume that the bootstrap assumptions hold in $\mathcal{R}^{III}_{u_{1},V_{1}}$ and we prove the desired improved estimates.

#### Preliminary Estimates

As a consequence of the bootstrap assumptions, we get the bounds:

$$ \frac{1}{2}\bigg|\frac{V\underline{v}}{u}\bigg|^{-\frac{p}{2}}\leq\bar{\Omega}^{2},\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\leq 2\bigg|\frac{V\underline{v}}{u}\bigg|^{\frac{p}{2}},\ \frac{1}{8}\leq|\partial_{V}r|\leq\frac{1}{2},\ \big|\partial_{u}r\big|\leq 2\bigg|\frac{V}{u}\bigg|^{\frac{p}{2}} $$

#### Lemma 3.9.

The area radius function satisfies the following:

$$ r(u,V)=\frac{V}{4}-u+O(\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}V) $$

In particular, we also have $V/8\leq r\leq V/2.$

#### Proof.

The proof follows from (3.39) and the estimate for $r$ on the spacelike hypersurface $\{u=-\underline{v}V\}.$ ∎

#### Main Estimates

We begin by improving assumption (3.37). Using the bootstrap assumptions, the preliminary estimates, and the estimates on the spacelike hypersurface $\big\{u=-\underline{v}V\big\},$ we have from (1.7):

$$ \displaystyle\big|r\partial_{V}\phi\big|(u,V) \displaystyle\leq\big|r\partial_{V}\phi\big|(-\underline{v}V,V)+\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}\big|\partial_{V}r\cdot\partial_{u}\phi\big|(u^{\prime},V)du^{\prime} \displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{2}\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon}+O\bigg(\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon}\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}V^{-1}\cdot\bigg|\frac{u^{\prime}}{V}\bigg|^{-p}du^{\prime}\bigg). $$

As a result, we have that

$$ \big|r\partial_{V}\phi\big|(u,V)\leq\frac{1}{2}\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon}+O\big(\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon}\underline{v}^{1-p}\big)\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\epsilon}. $$

Since $V\leq 8r,$ we improved the assumption (3.37) and proved (3.42).

Next, we improve the assumption (3.38). We can rewrite the wave equation as:

$$ \partial_{V}\bigg(\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg)=-\frac{p}{V}\cdot\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}r\partial_{u}\phi-\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}\partial_{u}r\partial_{V}\phi $$

We multiply the equation in order to obtain:

$$ \partial_{V}\bigg(\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg)^{2}+\frac{2p}{V}\cdot\bigg(\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg)^{2}=-2\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{2p}\partial_{u}r\partial_{V}\phi\cdot r\partial_{u}\phi $$

We integrate this equation and absorb an error term to obtain the energy estimate:

$$ \bigg(\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg)^{2}(u,V)+p\int_{-\frac{u}{\underline{v}}}^{V}\frac{1}{V^{\prime}}\cdot\bigg(\bigg|\frac{u}{V^{\prime}}\bigg|^{p}r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg)^{2}dV^{\prime}\\
\leq\big|\underline{v}^{p}r\partial_{u}\phi\big|^{2}\bigg(u,\frac{-u}{\underline{v}}\bigg)+p^{-1}\int_{-\frac{u}{\underline{v}}}^{V}V^{\prime}\cdot\bigg(\bigg|\frac{u}{V^{\prime}}\bigg|^{p}\partial_{u}r\partial_{V}\phi\bigg)^{2}dV^{\prime}. $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions, the preliminary estimates, and the bounds of the solution on $\big\{u=-\underline{v}V\big\}$ , we get

$$ \bigg(\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{p}r\partial_{u}\phi\bigg)^{2}\leq\frac{1}{2}\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}+O\bigg(\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}p^{-1}\int_{-\frac{u}{\underline{v}}}^{V}(V^{\prime})^{-1}\cdot\bigg|\frac{u}{V^{\prime}}\bigg|^{p}dV^{\prime}\bigg)\leq\frac{1}{2}\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}+O\bigg(\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\underline{v}^{p}\bigg)\leq\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}. $$

Since $V\leq 8r,$ we improved the assumption Eq. 3.38 by using the smallness of $\underline{v}$ .

In the following, we will improve assumption (3.39). We can rewrite the wave equation (1.6) for $r$ as:

$$ \partial_{u}\bigg(r\bigg(\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg)\bigg)=-\frac{\bar{\Omega}^{2}}{4}\cdot\big(\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{u}r+1\big) $$

We integrate this and use the bootstrap assumptions, the preliminary estimates, and the bounds of the solution on $\{u=-\underline{v}V\}$ in order to get:

$$ r\bigg|\partial_{V}r-\frac{1}{4}\bigg|\leq\frac{1}{2}V\kappa^{1-\epsilon}+O\bigg(\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}\bigg|\frac{V}{u^{\prime}}\bigg|^{\frac{p}{2}}du^{\prime}\bigg)\leq\frac{1}{2}V\kappa^{1-\epsilon}+O\big(V\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\underline{v}^{1-\frac{p}{2}}\big)\leq V\kappa^{1-2\epsilon} $$

Using $v\leq 8r$ again, we improved the assumption (3.39) and proved (3.44).

We improve the assumption (3.40). We have from the Raychaudhuri equation (1.8):

$$ \big|\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{u}r+1\big|(u,V)\leq\big|\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{u}r+1\big|(-\underline{v}V,V)+\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}r\bar{\Omega}^{-2}(\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}(u^{\prime},V)du^{\prime} $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions and the preliminary estimates, the second term can be bounded as follows:

$$ \displaystyle\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}r\bar{\Omega}^{-2}(\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}(u^{\prime},V)du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim V^{-1}\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}\bigg(V\bigg|\frac{u^{\prime}}{V}\bigg|^{p}\big|\partial_{u}\phi\big|\bigg)^{2}\cdot\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\cdot\bigg|\frac{u^{\prime}}{V}\bigg|^{-2p}du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}V^{-1}\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}\bigg|\frac{u^{\prime}}{V}\bigg|^{-\frac{5}{2}p}\underline{v}^{\frac{p}{2}}du^{\prime}\lesssim\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\underline{v}^{1-2p} $$

since $2p<1.$ Using this, the estimates on the spacelike hypersurface $\{u=-\underline{v}V\}$ , and the smallness of $\underline{v}$ , we get

$$ \big|\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\partial_{u}r+1\big|(u,V)\leq 10\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}. $$

Thus, we improved the assumption (3.40) and proved (3.45).

Finally, we improve the assumption (3.41). As in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ , an essential step is obtaining estimates on the Hawking mass. We have from (3.33):

$$ m(u,V)\leq m\bigg(u,-\frac{u}{\underline{v}}\bigg)+\int_{-\frac{u}{\underline{v}}}^{V}\big(2\partial_{V}r\big)^{-1}\cdot\bigg(1-\frac{2m}{r}\bigg)\cdot r^{2}(\partial_{V}\phi)^{2}dV^{\prime} $$

Using the bootstrap assumptions, the preliminary estimates, and the estimate for $m$ in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ , we get:

$$ m(u,V)\leq\kappa^{1-\epsilon}\bigg|\frac{u}{\underline{v}}\bigg|+O\bigg(\int_{-\frac{u}{\underline{v}}}^{V}\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}dV^{\prime}\bigg)\lesssim V\kappa^{1-2\epsilon} $$

As a result, we obtain that:

$$ \frac{m}{r}(u,V)=O\big(\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\big) $$

We use this estimate in (3.34), and we get:

$$ \partial_{u}\partial_{V}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}=O\bigg(\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}V^{-2}\bigg|\frac{u}{V}\bigg|^{-p}\bigg) $$

We integrate this and use the estimate (3.35) for $\partial_{u}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}$ in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ :

$$ \partial_{u}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}(u,v)=\partial_{u}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\bigg(u,-\frac{u}{\underline{v}}\bigg)+O\bigg(\int_{-\frac{u}{\underline{v}}}^{V}\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}|u|^{-p}(V^{\prime})^{-2+p}dV^{\prime}\bigg)=O\big(\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\underline{v}^{1-p}|u|^{-1}\big). $$

Once again, we integrate this and use the estimate (3.36) for $\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}$ in region $\mathcal{R}_{II}$ :

$$ \big|\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big|(u,V)\leq\big|\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big|(-\underline{v}V,V)+O\bigg(\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\underline{v}^{1-p}|u^{\prime}|^{-1}du^{\prime}\bigg)\leq\kappa^{1-2\epsilon}\bigg(1+\log\bigg|\frac{V\underline{v}}{u}\bigg|\bigg), $$

where we also used the smallness of $\underline{v}.$ In conclusion, we also improved the assumption (3.41), completing the proof of Proposition 3.8. ∎

### 3.4 Region $\mathcal{R}_{IV}$

In this section we prove existence of the solution in region $\mathcal{R}_{IV}$ and use the obtained estimates to complete the proof of Theorem 1, by showing that the constructed spacetime has an incomplete $\mathcal{I}^{+}.$ In the double null coordinates $(u,V)$ , we have that region $\mathcal{R}_{IV}$ is given by:

$$ \mathcal{R}_{IV}=\bigg\{(u,V):\ u\in[-1,0),\ V\in[1,\infty),\ \frac{V}{|u|}\geq\underline{v}^{-1}\bigg\} $$

To simplify our analysis, we split region $\mathcal{R}_{IV}$ into the following two sub-regions:

$$ \mathcal{R}_{IV}=\big(\mathcal{R}_{IV}\cap\{V\leq\underline{v}^{-1}\}\big)\cup[-1,0)\times[\underline{v}^{-1},\infty) $$

We first prove existence of the solution in the first sub-region:

#### Proposition 3.10.

We denote $\eta=10\epsilon.$ The solution constructed in Proposition 3.7 extends to region $\mathcal{R}_{IV}$ for $V\leq\underline{v}^{-1}$ , and satisfies the following estimates:

$$ \displaystyle|m| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{1-\epsilon} \displaystyle|\partial_{u}r| \displaystyle\leq 10|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}} \displaystyle\big|4\partial_{V}r-1\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{1-\eta} \displaystyle\big|\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{1-3\eta}\big(1-\log|u|\big) \displaystyle|r\phi| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\eta} \displaystyle\big|r\partial_{V}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\eta} \displaystyle\big|r\partial_{u}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\eta}|u|^{-p} $$

#### Proof.

For any $(u_{1},V_{1})\in\mathcal{R}_{IV}\cap\{V\leq\underline{v}^{-1}\},$ we assume that the solution satisfies the following bootstrap assumptions for all $(u,V)\in\mathcal{R}^{IV}_{u_{1},V_{1}}=\big([-1,u_{1}]\times[0,V_{1}]\big)\cap\mathcal{R}_{IV}\cap\{V\leq\underline{v}^{-1}\}:$

$$ |\phi|\leq 1,\ |\partial_{u}r|\leq 100|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}},\ \frac{1}{8}\leq\partial_{V}r\leq\frac{1}{2},\ \bar{\Omega}^{2},\bar{\Omega}^{-2}\leq 100|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}} $$

We remark that the bootstrap assumptions hold initially, since the solution satisfies the following estimates on $\big\{u\in[-\underline{v},0),V=1\big\}\cup\big\{V\in[1,\underline{v}^{-1}],\ u=-\underline{v}V\big\}:$

$$ |\partial_{u}r|\leq 4|u|^{-\frac{p}{10}},\ \big|4\partial_{V}r-1\big|\leq\kappa^{1-\frac{\eta}{2}},\ \big|\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big|\leq\kappa^{1-\frac{\eta}{2}}\big(1-\log|u|\big) $$

$$ |r\phi|\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\eta}{2}},\ \big|r\partial_{V}\phi\big|\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\eta}{2}},\ \big|r\partial_{u}\phi\big|\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\eta}{2}}|u|^{-p} $$

In the above, the bound for $r\phi$ follows since $\phi(p)=0$ and using our previous bounds for $\partial_{u}\phi,\ \partial_{V}\phi.$ To complete the proof, it suffices to prove that the estimates (3.49)–(3.55) hold in $\mathcal{R}^{IV}_{u_{1},V_{1}}.$ Using the bootstrap assumption on $\partial_{V}r$ , we obtain that in $\mathcal{R}^{IV}_{u_{1},V_{1}}$ the radius function satisfies $r\sim V.$ We first remark that the monotonicity properties of the Hawking mass and the bound on $C_{0}^{+}$ imply (3.49). We use this in the equation:

$$ \partial_{u}\partial_{V}r=-\frac{\bar{\Omega}^{2}\cdot m}{2r^{2}} $$

in order to obtain the estimate:

$$ \partial_{V}r=\frac{1}{4}+O(\kappa^{1-\frac{\eta}{2}})+O\bigg(\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}\kappa^{1-\epsilon}V^{-2}|u^{\prime}|^{-\frac{p}{2}}du^{\prime}\bigg)=\frac{1}{4}+O(\kappa^{1-\frac{\eta}{2}}) $$

which proves (3.51). Similarly, we prove (3.50) by the estimate:

$$ |\partial_{u}r|\leq 4|u|^{-\frac{p}{10}}+O\bigg(\int_{\max(1,-\underline{v}u)}^{V}\kappa^{1-\epsilon}(V^{\prime})^{-2}|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}}dV^{\prime}\bigg)\leq 10|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}} $$

Next, we rewrite the wave equation (1.7) as:

$$ \partial_{u}\partial_{V}(r\phi)=-\frac{\bar{\Omega}^{2}\cdot m\cdot\phi}{2r^{2}} $$

As a result, we obtain the bound

$$ \big|\partial_{u}(r\phi)\big|\leq C\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\eta}{2}}|u|^{-p}+O\bigg(\int_{\max(1,-\underline{v}u)}^{V}\kappa^{1-\epsilon}(V^{\prime})^{-2}|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}}dV^{\prime}\bigg)\leq 2C\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\eta}{2}}|u|^{-p}. $$

We integrate this bound in the $u$ direction to prove (3.53). Moreover, we also have

$$ \big|r\partial_{u}\phi\big|\leq 2C\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\eta}{2}}|u|^{-p}+\big|\phi\partial_{u}r\big|\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\eta}|u|^{-p} $$

which proves (3.55). Similarly, we prove (3.54):

$$ \big|r\partial_{V}\phi\big|\leq C\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\eta}{2}}+|\phi\partial_{V}r|+O\bigg(\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}\kappa^{1-\epsilon}V^{-2}|u^{\prime}|^{-\frac{p}{2}}du^{\prime}\bigg)\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\eta}. $$

Using equation (3.34) and the previously established bounds, we obtain the estimate

$$ \big|\partial_{V}\log\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big|\leq\kappa^{1-\frac{\eta}{2}}+O\bigg(\int_{-\underline{v}V}^{u}\kappa^{1-2\eta}V^{-2}|u^{\prime}|^{-p}du^{\prime}\bigg)\leq\kappa^{1-\frac{5}{2}\eta}. $$

Finally, we integrate this bound using the estimate on the initial data, in order to obtain (3.52). ∎

We now prove existence of the solution in the second sub-region:

#### Proposition 3.11.

The solution constructed in Proposition 3.10 extends to $\big\{u\in[-1,0),\ V\in[\underline{v},\infty)\big\}$ , and satisfies the following estimates:

$$ \displaystyle|m| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{1-\epsilon} \displaystyle|\partial_{u}r| \displaystyle\leq 20|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}} \displaystyle\big|4V^{\kappa}\partial_{V}r-1\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{1-2\eta} \displaystyle\big|\log V^{\kappa}\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{1-5\eta}\big(1-\log|u|\big) \displaystyle|\phi| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-2\eta} \displaystyle\big|rV^{\kappa}\partial_{V}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-2\eta} \displaystyle\big|r\partial_{u}\phi\big| \displaystyle\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-2\eta}|u|^{-p} $$

#### Proof.

For any $(u_{1},V_{1})\in[-1,0)\times[\underline{v},\infty),$ we assume that the solution satisfies the following bootstrap assumptions for all $(u,V)\in[-1,u_{1}]\times[\underline{v},V_{1}]$ :

$$ |\phi|\leq 1,\ |\partial_{u}r|\leq 100|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}},\ \frac{1}{8}\leq V^{\kappa}\partial_{V}r\leq\frac{1}{2},\ V^{\kappa}\bar{\Omega}^{2}\leq 100|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}}. $$

The bootstrap assumptions hold initially because of the estimates in Proposition 3.10 and the bounds on the initial data on $C_{0}^{+}.$ To complete the proof, we prove that the estimates (3.56)–(3.62) hold in $[-1,u_{1}]\times[\underline{v},V_{1}].$ Using the bootstrap assumption on $\partial_{V}r$ , we obtain that in $[-1,u_{1}]\times[\underline{v},V_{1}]$ the radius function satisfies $r\sim V^{1-\kappa}.$ As before, (3.56) follows from the monotonicity properties of the Hawking mass and the bound on $C_{0}^{+}$ . We use this bound in the equation

$$ \partial_{u}\big(V^{\kappa}\partial_{V}r\big)=-\frac{\bar{\Omega}^{2}\cdot m\cdot V^{\kappa}}{2r^{2}} $$

in order to obtain the estimate

$$ V^{\kappa}\partial_{V}r=\frac{1}{4}+O(\kappa^{1-\eta})+O\bigg(\int_{-1}^{u}\kappa^{1-\epsilon}V^{-2+2\kappa}|u^{\prime}|^{-\frac{p}{2}}du^{\prime}\bigg)=\frac{1}{4}+O(\kappa^{1-\eta}) $$

which proves (3.58). Similarly, we prove (3.57) using

$$ |\partial_{u}r|\leq 10|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}}+O\bigg(\int_{\underline{v}}^{V}\kappa^{1-\epsilon}(V^{\prime})^{-2+\kappa}|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}}dV^{\prime}\bigg)\leq 20|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}}. $$

Next, we use (1.7) to obtain the bound

$$ \big|\partial_{u}(r\phi)\big|\leq C\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\eta}|u|^{-p}+O\bigg(\int_{\underline{v}}^{V}\kappa^{1-\epsilon}(V^{\prime})^{-2+\kappa}|u|^{-\frac{p}{2}}dV^{\prime}\bigg)\leq 2C\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\eta}|u|^{-p} $$

We integrate in the $u$ direction and divide by $r$ in order to prove (3.60). Moreover, we also have

$$ \big|r\partial_{u}\phi\big|\leq 2C\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\eta}|u|^{-p}+\big|\phi\partial_{u}r\big|\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-2\eta}|u|^{-p} $$

which proves (3.62). Similarly, we prove (3.61):

$$ \big|rV^{\kappa}\partial_{V}\phi\big|\leq C\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\eta}{2}}+|\phi V^{\kappa}\partial_{V}r|+O\bigg(\int_{-1}^{u}\kappa^{1-\epsilon}V^{-2+2\kappa}|u^{\prime}|^{-\frac{p}{2}}du^{\prime}\bigg)\leq\kappa^{\frac{1}{2}-2\eta}. $$

Using equation (3.34) and the previously established bounds, we obtain

$$ \big|\partial_{V}\log V^{\kappa}\bar{\Omega}^{2}\big|=O\bigg(\int_{-1}^{u}\kappa^{1-4\eta}V^{-2+\kappa}|u^{\prime}|^{-p}du^{\prime}\bigg)=O\big(\kappa^{1-4\eta}V^{-2+\kappa}\big). $$

Since we obtain enough decay in $V,$ we integrate this bound and use (3.52) to obtain (3.59). ∎

### 3.5 Proof of Theorem 1

Finally, the estimates that we proved so far allow us to complete the proof of Theorem 1:

#### Proof of Theorem 1.

By construction, the solution satisfies the discrete self-similarity conditions (1.3) on $C_{0}^{-}$ . Our analysis of the solution in regions $\mathcal{R}_{I},\mathcal{R}_{II},\mathcal{R}_{III},$ and $\mathcal{R}_{IV}$ proves that the solution exists in the exterior region $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{Ext}}$ . Moreover, the affine length of $\mathcal{I}^{+}$ is given (see [Daf05a]) by

$$ \lim_{v\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-1}^{0}\frac{\Omega^{2}(u,v)}{\Omega^{2}(-1,v)}du=\lim_{V\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-1}^{0}\frac{\bar{\Omega}^{2}(u,V)}{\bar{\Omega}^{2}(-1,V)}du=\lim_{V\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-1}^{0}V^{\kappa}\bar{\Omega}^{2}(u,V)du. $$

We use the bound (3.59) in order to get:

$$ \lim_{V\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-1}^{0}V^{\kappa}\bar{\Omega}^{2}(u,V)du\leq\lim_{V\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-1}^{0}e^{\kappa^{1-5\eta}}|u|^{-p}du\lesssim 1. $$

In conclusion, the spacetime $\big(M,g\big)$ has a future incomplete $\mathcal{I}^{+}$ . ∎

# Weak cosmic censorship for the circularly symmetric Einstein-scalar field system in $2+1$ dimensions

**Authors:** Serban Cicortas Note: Princeton University, Department of Mathematics, Fine Hall, Washington Road, Princeton, NJ 08544, USA

## Abstract

We prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions for the circularly symmetric Einstein-scalar field system in the presence of a negative cosmological constant $\Lambda<0$ . More precisely, we show that for any integer $k\geq 2$ , the maximal development of generic $C^{k}$ initial data does not contain naked singularities. An essential step of the proof is establishing the presence of a mass gap. In particular, this implies that all naked singularities have infinite blueshift, which represents the main instability mechanism.
