For any $(u,r_{0})\in\mathcal{D},$ we parametrize the future directed ingoing null curve passing through $(u,r_{0})$ as:

$$ \chi_{u,r_{0}}(s)=\bigg(s,r_{0}-\frac{1}{2}\int_{u}^{s}\overline{\gamma}\big(\chi_{u,r_{0}}(s^{\prime})\big)ds^{\prime}\bigg), $$

with $s\in\big[u,u_{\Gamma}(u,r_{0})\big]$ , such that $\chi_{u,r_{0}}(u)=(u,r_{0})$ and $\chi_{u,r_{0}}\big(u_{\Gamma}(u,r_{0})\big)\in\Gamma.$ We note that $\chi_{u,r_{0}}$ has tangent vector $n.$ For example, the ingoing cone $C_{*}^{-}$ is parametrized as $\{\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(s):\ s\in[u_{0},u_{*})\}.$ See Figure 4 for an illustration of this notation.

*Figure 4: Points $(u_{0},r_{0}),\ \chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u),$ and $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}\big(u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},r_{0})\big)$ in the domain $\mathcal{D}$ .*

We also introduce the following notation:

$$ r\big(\chi_{u,r_{0}}(s)\big):=r_{0}-\frac{1}{2}\int_{u}^{s}\overline{\gamma}\big(\chi_{u,r_{0}}(s^{\prime})\big)ds^{\prime}. $$

Using this notation, we can rewrite $\mathcal{D}$ as follows:

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{D} \displaystyle=\Big\{(u,r)\in\mathcal{Q}:\ u_{0}\leq u<u_{*},\ 0\leq r\leq r\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(u)\big)\Big\} \displaystyle=\Big\{\chi_{u_{0},r}(u)\in\mathcal{Q}:\ 0\leq r\leq r_{*},\ u_{0}\leq u\leq u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},r)\Big\}. $$

In practice, we also use truncated domains. For any $0<r_{1}\leq r_{*}$ and $u_{0}<u_{1}\leq u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},r_{1}),$ we define:

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}} \displaystyle=\Big\{(u,r):\ u_{0}\leq u\leq u_{1},\ 0\leq r\leq r\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{1}}(u)\big)\Big\} \displaystyle=\Big\{\chi_{u_{0},r}(u)\in\mathcal{Q}:\ 0\leq r\leq r_{1},\ u_{0}\leq u\leq\min\big(u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},r),u_{1}\big)\Big\}. $$

This domain represents the intersection of: the future of $C_{0}^{+}$ , the past of the outgoing cone $\{u=u_{1}\}$ , and the past of the ingoing cone passing through $(u_{0},r_{1}).$

### 3.2 Bounds on the geometry

In this section, we derive a series of pointwise bounds on the quantities $\lambda,\nu,\gamma,\overline{\gamma}$ (together with their derivatives), as a consequence of the mass estimate $0\leq m\leq 1-\delta$ in $\mathcal{D}.$ At the end of the section, we also define the volume forms used in our argument.

Shrinking the domain $\mathcal{D}$ if necessary (by increasing $u_{0}$ ), we can assume that $r_{*}$ satisfies:

$$ r_{*}\leq\frac{\delta^{3}}{1000(1+|\Lambda|)(1+|u_{*}-u_{0}|)}\text{ and }r_{*}\leq\frac{1}{1000}. $$

Firstly, (3.4) implies that:

$$ e^{2\lambda}\leq\frac{1}{\delta+|\Lambda|r^{2}}. $$

As a consequence, (3.8) implies that:

$$ 0\leq\partial_{r}\big(\nu-\lambda\big)\leq\frac{2r|\Lambda|}{\delta+|\Lambda|r^{2}}=\frac{d}{dr}\log\bigg(1+\frac{|\Lambda|}{\delta}r^{2}\bigg). $$

We integrate this equation, using the boundary conditions at $\Gamma,$ to obtain:

$$ 1\leq\overline{\gamma}\leq 1+\frac{|\Lambda|}{\delta}r^{2}. $$

Since $\gamma=2e^{2\lambda}\overline{\gamma},$ the estimates (3.14)-(3.15) imply:

$$ 2\leq\gamma\leq\frac{2}{\delta}. $$

We derive further bounds for the derivatives of $\overline{\gamma}$ using (3.7), (3.8), and (3.16):

$$ \partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}=|\Lambda|r\gamma\leq\frac{2|\Lambda|}{\delta}\cdot r $$

$$ \partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}=|\Lambda|\gamma\Big(1+r^{2}(\partial_{r}\phi)^{2}\Big)\leq\frac{2|\Lambda|}{\delta}\Big(1+r^{2}(\partial_{r}\phi)^{2}\Big) $$

We introduce the following notation, which will be used in the definition of volume forms:

$$ \textbf{v}(u,r_{0},s):=\frac{d}{dr_{0}}r\big(\chi_{u,r_{0}}(s)\big). $$

According to (3.11), we have for any $s\in\big[u,u_{\Gamma}(u,r_{0})\big]$ :

$$ \textbf{v}(u,r_{0},s)=1-\frac{1}{2}\int_{u}^{s}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\chi_{u,r_{0}}(s^{\prime})\big)\cdot\textbf{v}(u,r_{0},s^{\prime})ds^{\prime}. $$

Thus, we have the estimate:

$$ \big|\textbf{v}(u,r_{0},s)\big|\leq 1+\frac{1}{2}\int_{u}^{s}\Big|\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\chi_{u,r_{0}}(s^{\prime})\big)\Big|\cdot\big|\textbf{v}(u,r_{0},s^{\prime})\big|ds^{\prime}. $$

Using Grönwall’s inequality, (3.17), and (3.13), we get that $\big|\textbf{v}(u,r_{0},s)\big|<2.$ We further get that:

$$ \big|\textbf{v}(u,r_{0},s)-1\big|\leq\int_{u}^{s}\Big|\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\chi_{u,r_{0}}(s^{\prime})\big)\Big|ds^{\prime}\leq\frac{2|\Lambda|r_{*}|u_{*}-u_{0}|}{\delta}<\frac{1}{50}. $$

For any $0<r_{1}\leq r_{*}$ and $u_{0}<u_{1}\leq u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},r_{1}),$ we consider the truncated domain $\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ defined in (3.12). For any quantity $E$ that is defined on $\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ , we denote its integral over $\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ by:

$$ \displaystyle\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}}E\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle=\int_{0}^{r_{1}}\int_{u_{0}}^{\min\{u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},\tilde{r}),u_{1}\}}E\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(u)\big)\cdot\textbf{v}(u_{0},\tilde{r},u)dud\tilde{r} \displaystyle=\int_{u_{0}}^{u_{1}}\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{1}}(u))}E(u,r)drdu. $$

### 3.3 Preliminary estimates for the scalar field

In this section, we establish preliminary estimates for the scalar field. In particular, we show in (3.23) that the scalar field cannot blow up at a rate that is faster than the self-similar rate. First, using (3.10) and (3.14), we have the following a priori bound for the energy of the scalar field for any $(u,r)\in\mathcal{D}$ :

$$ \int_{0}^{r}\tilde{r}\big(\partial_{r}\phi\big)^{2}(u,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\leq\frac{m(u,r)}{\delta}. $$

We define $\psi=r^{3/2}\partial_{r}\phi.$ Since $k\geq 2,$ (2.18)-(2.19) imply that there exists a constant $A>0$ , such that:

$$ \sup_{r\in[0,r_{*}]}\big|\partial_{r}\phi(u_{0},r)\big|^{2}+\int_{0}^{r_{*}}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\leq\frac{A^{2}}{1000}. $$

We state the main result of the section:

#### Proposition 3.1.

We have the following estimates for the scalar field:

$$ \sup_{(u,r)\in\mathcal{D}}\big|r\partial_{r}\phi(u,r)\big|\leq A, $$

$$ \sup_{u\in[u_{0},u_{*})}\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(u))}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr+\iint_{\mathcal{D}}\bigg(\frac{\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}}{r}+\frac{\psi^{2}}{r^{3}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq A^{2}. $$

We first derive the following identity for $\psi,$ which is essential in proving energy estimates:

#### Lemma 3.1.

The function $\psi=r^{3/2}\partial_{r}\phi$ satisfies the identity:

$$ n\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{1}{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}-\frac{3}{8r^{2}}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\big(\psi^{2}\big)-2\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\psi\partial_{r}\psi\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{r}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}-\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}\bigg)=0. $$

#### Proof.

The wave equation (3.6) implies:

$$ 2\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\big(r\partial_{r}\phi\big)+\frac{1}{r}\partial_{u}\big(r\partial_{r}\phi\big)-\partial_{r}^{2}\big(r\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\phi\big)=0. $$

Using the definition of $\psi$ , we get that:

$$ 2\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\psi-r^{1/2}\partial_{r}^{2}\big(r^{-1/2}\overline{\gamma}\psi\big)=0. $$

Expanding the second term, we further get that:

$$ 2\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\psi-\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}^{2}\psi-2\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\psi+\frac{1}{r}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\psi-\frac{3}{4r^{2}}\overline{\gamma}\psi-\psi\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}+\frac{1}{r}\psi\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}=0. $$

Next, we use (3.5) to get the equation:

$$ 2n\partial_{r}\psi+\frac{1}{r}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\psi-\frac{3}{4r^{2}}\overline{\gamma}\psi-2\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\psi+\frac{1}{r}\psi\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}-\psi\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}=0. $$

Multiplying by $\partial_{r}\psi,$ we conclude the proof of (3.25). ∎

#### Proof of Proposition 3.1.

For some $0<r_{1}\leq r_{*}$ and $u_{0}<u_{1}\leq u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},r_{1}),$ we make the bootstrap assumption for all $(u,r)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ :

$$ \big|\partial_{r}\phi(u,r)\big|\leq\frac{A}{r}. $$

We note that a direct computation using (3.19) implies that:

$$ n\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(s)\big)\cdot\textbf{v}(u_{0},\tilde{r},s)=\frac{d}{ds}\bigg(\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(s)\big)\cdot\textbf{v}(u_{0},\tilde{r},s)\bigg)+\frac{1}{2}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(s)\big)\cdot\textbf{v}(u_{0},\tilde{r},s). $$

For any $\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ we integrate (3.25) along $\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}$ for $s\in[u_{0},u]:$

$$ \big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(u)\big)\cdot\textbf{v}(u_{0},\tilde{r},u)+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\bigg(\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{r}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(s)\big)-\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2}}\partial_{r}\psi^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(s)\big)\bigg)\cdot\textbf{v}(u_{0},\tilde{r},s)ds= $$

$$ =\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\bigg(\frac{3}{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(s)\big)+\psi\partial_{r}\psi\cdot\bigg(\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}-\frac{1}{r}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\bigg)\big(\chi_{u_{0},\tilde{r}}(s)\big)\bigg)\cdot\textbf{v}(u_{0},\tilde{r},s)ds. $$

We notice that for $k\geq 2,$ (2.19) implies that $\partial_{r}\psi=0$ on $\Gamma.$ For any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}},$ we integrate the identity for all $\tilde{r}\in[0,r_{0}]:$

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u))}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{r}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}-\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2}}\partial_{r}\psi^{2}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle=\int_{0}^{r_{0}}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{3}{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\psi\partial_{r}\psi\bigg(\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}-\frac{1}{r}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\bigg)\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

We deal with the following error term by integration by parts, since $r^{-1}\psi=0$ on $\Gamma$ :

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2}}\partial_{r}\psi^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}=\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2}}\psi^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{4r^{3}}-\frac{3\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2}}\bigg)\psi^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

We have the following Hardy inequality, again using $r^{-1}\psi=0$ on $\Gamma$ :

$$ \frac{\overline{\gamma}\psi^{2}}{r^{2}}(s,r)+\int_{0}^{r}\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{\tilde{r}^{3}}\psi^{2}(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\leq\int_{0}^{r}\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{\tilde{r}}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}+\int_{0}^{r}\frac{\psi^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{\tilde{r}^{2}}(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}. $$

We use (3.29) for $(s,r)=\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)$ in (3.28) to get that:

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2}}\partial_{r}\psi^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{4r}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{3\psi^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

As a consequence of (3.29), we also have the estimate:

$$ \frac{1}{8}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{r^{3}}\psi^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{1}{8}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{r}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{\psi^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{r^{2}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

Next, we consider the following error term and use (3.18):

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\psi\partial_{r}\psi\cdot\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}\ d\mathrm{Vol}=\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\gamma\bigg(\psi\partial_{r}\psi+\frac{\partial_{r}\psi^{4}}{4r}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

We integrate by parts the second term to obtain:

$$ \displaystyle\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\partial_{r}\psi^{4}}{4r}\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle=\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\psi^{4}\bigg(\frac{\gamma}{4r^{2}}-\frac{\partial_{r}\gamma}{4r}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\psi^{4}}{4r}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds \displaystyle\leq\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\psi^{4}\frac{\gamma}{4r^{2}}\ d\mathrm{Vol}+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\psi^{4}}{4r}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds. $$

The error term estimates (3.30)-(3.32) and the energy identity (3.27) imply for any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u))} \displaystyle\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{r}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{r^{3}}\psi^{2}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle\leq 16 \displaystyle\int_{0}^{r_{0}}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}+16\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{\psi^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{r^{2}}+|\Lambda|\gamma\cdot|\psi\partial_{r}\psi|\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle+16\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\psi^{4}\frac{\gamma}{4r^{2}}\ d\mathrm{Vol}+16\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\psi^{4}}{4r}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds. $$

We use (3.16) and (3.17) to bound the error terms:

$$ \displaystyle\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{\psi^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{r^{2}}+|\Lambda|\gamma\cdot|\psi\partial_{r}\psi|\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle\leq\frac{4|\Lambda|}{\delta}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(r\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{\psi^{2}}{r}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle\leq\frac{4|\Lambda|}{\delta}r_{*}^{2}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}}{r}+\frac{\psi^{2}}{r^{3}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}, $$

which can be absorbed on the LHS of the energy estimate using (3.13) and (3.15). We use the bootstrap assumption (3.26), the preliminary estimate (3.21), and (3.13):

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\psi^{4}\frac{\gamma}{4r^{2}}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{|\Lambda|A^{2}}{2\delta}r_{*}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{\psi^{2}}{r^{2}}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{|\Lambda|A^{2}|u-u_{0}|\cdot m(u_{0},r_{0})\cdot r_{*}}{2\delta^{2}}\leq\frac{A^{2}}{1000}. $$

Additionally, using Cauchy-Schwarz and (3.21), we also have:

$$ \psi^{4}(s,r)=\bigg(2\int_{0}^{r}\psi\partial_{r}\psi(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\bigg)^{2}\leq\frac{4m(s,r)}{\delta}\int_{0}^{r}\tilde{r}^{2}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}. $$

We use this for $(s,r)=\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)$ to get for the last error term in (3.33):

$$ \int_{u_{0}}^{u}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\psi^{4}}{4r}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds\leq\frac{4|\Lambda|}{\delta^{2}}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{4|\Lambda|}{\delta^{2}}r_{*}^{2}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}}{r}\ d\mathrm{Vol}, $$

which can again be absorbed on the LHS of the energy estimate.

We bounded all the error terms in (3.33), so using (3.22) for the initial data, we proved that for any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ we have the estimate:

$$ \int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u))}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}}{r}+\frac{\psi^{2}}{r^{3}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{A^{2}}{10}. $$

Using the first term in (3.34), we can improve the bootstrap assumption (3.26) for all $(u,r)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ :

$$ \big|r\partial_{r}\phi\big|(u,r)\leq\frac{1}{r^{1/2}}\int_{0}^{r}\big|\partial_{r}\psi\big|(u,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\leq\bigg(\int_{0}^{r}\big|\partial_{r}\psi\big|^{2}(u,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\bigg)^{1/2}\leq\frac{A}{2}. $$

Thus, we conclude that (3.26) and (3.34) hold for all $0<r_{1}\leq r_{*}$ and $u_{0}<u_{1}\leq u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},r_{1}),$ completing the proof of (3.23)-(3.24). ∎

### 3.4 Improved estimates for the scalar field

The goal of this section is to improve the previous preliminary estimates. The main point is that we had additional room for improvement in the proof of Proposition 3.1, which we exploit in Proposition 3.2. The improved estimates will play a key role in Section 3.5 and allow us to prove uniform bounds for the local well-posedness norm.

We fix $\rho=1/100.$ Since $k\geq 2,$ (2.18)-(2.19) imply that there exists a constant $\tilde{A}>0$ , such that:

$$ \int_{0}^{r_{*}}\tilde{r}^{-\rho}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\leq\frac{\tilde{A}^{2}}{1000}. $$

#### Proposition 3.2.

We have the following estimates for the scalar field:

$$ \sup_{(u,r)\in\mathcal{D}}\big|r^{1-\frac{\rho}{2}}\partial_{r}\phi(u,r)\big|\leq A+\tilde{A}, $$

$$ \sup_{u\in[u_{0},u_{*})}\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(u))}r^{-\rho}(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr+\iint_{\mathcal{D}}\bigg(\frac{\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}}{r^{1+\rho}}+\frac{\psi^{2}}{r^{3+\rho}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq A^{2}+\tilde{A}^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

The proof mirrors that of Proposition 3.1. We multiply (3.25) with $r^{-\rho}$ to get:

$$ n\Big(r^{-\rho}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}\Big)+\frac{1-\rho/2}{r^{1+\rho}}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}-\frac{3}{8r^{2+\rho}}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\psi^{2}-2r^{-\rho}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+r^{-\rho}\psi\partial_{r}\psi\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{r}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}-\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}\bigg)=0. $$

As in the proof of Proposition 3.1, this implies the energy identity for any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}:$

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u))}r^{-\rho}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{1-\rho/2}{r^{1+\rho}}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}-\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2+\rho}}\partial_{r}\psi^{2}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle=\int_{0}^{r_{0}}\tilde{r}^{-\rho}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{3}{2}r^{-\rho}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+r^{-\rho}\psi\partial_{r}\psi\bigg(\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}-\frac{1}{r}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\bigg)\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

As before, we first deal with the following error term in (3.38) by integration by parts:

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2+\rho}}\partial_{r}\psi^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}=\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2+\rho}}\psi^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{3(2+\rho)\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{3+\rho}}-\frac{3\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2+\rho}}\bigg)\psi^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

Additionally, we have the following Hardy inequality:

$$ \frac{\overline{\gamma}\psi^{2}}{r^{2+\rho}}(s,r)+\int_{0}^{r}\frac{(1+\rho)\overline{\gamma}}{\tilde{r}^{3+\rho}}\psi^{2}(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\leq\int_{0}^{r}\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{\tilde{r}^{1+\rho}}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}+\int_{0}^{r}\frac{\psi^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{\tilde{r}^{2+\rho}}(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}. $$

Using (3.39), we obtain the following bound for the error terms:

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{3\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{2+\rho}}\partial_{r}\psi^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}+\frac{1}{8}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{\overline{\gamma}}{r^{3+\rho}}\psi^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{(7+3\rho)\overline{\gamma}}{8r^{1+\rho}}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{\psi^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{r^{2+\rho}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

Next, we consider the following error term in (3.38):

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r^{-\rho}\psi\partial_{r}\psi\cdot\partial_{r}^{2}\overline{\gamma}\ d\mathrm{Vol}=\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\gamma\bigg(r^{-\rho}\psi\partial_{r}\psi+\frac{\partial_{r}\psi^{4}}{4r^{1+\rho}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

We integrate by parts the second term to obtain:

$$ \displaystyle\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\partial_{r}\psi^{4}}{4r^{1+\rho}}\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle=\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\psi^{4}\bigg(\frac{(1+\rho)\gamma}{4r^{2+\rho}}-\frac{\partial_{r}\gamma}{4r^{1+\rho}}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\psi^{4}}{4r^{1+\rho}}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds \displaystyle\leq\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\psi^{4}\frac{(1+\rho)\gamma}{4r^{2+\rho}}\ d\mathrm{Vol}+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\psi^{4}}{4r^{1+\rho}}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds. $$

Using the error term estimates (3.40)-(3.41) and the energy identity (3.38), we get for any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u))} \displaystyle r^{-\rho}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(\frac{1}{r^{1+\rho}}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{1}{r^{3+\rho}}\psi^{2}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle\leq 32 \displaystyle\int_{0}^{r_{0}}\tilde{r}^{-\rho}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}+32\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(r^{-\rho}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\psi\big)^{2}+\frac{\psi^{2}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}}{r^{2+\rho}}+r^{-\rho}|\Lambda|\gamma\cdot|\psi\partial_{r}\psi|\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle+32\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}|\Lambda|\psi^{4}\frac{\gamma}{4r^{2+\rho}}\ d\mathrm{Vol}+32\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|\Lambda|\gamma\frac{\psi^{4}}{4r^{1+\rho}}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds. $$

The first term on the RHS is bounded by $\tilde{A}^{2}/10$ due to (3.35). We notice that the remaining error terms are bounded by $A^{2}/5.$ This follows since in the proof of Proposition 3.1 we had additional room left in the powers of $r$ used. Thus, we conclude that (3.36)-(3.37) hold. ∎

### 3.5 Proof of Theorem 1.2

#### Proof of Theorem 1.2.

To contradict Assumption 3.1 and complete the proof of Theorem 1.2, it suffices to show that for $I(u)=\{u\}\times\big[0,r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(u))\big],$ the functions $\phi\in H^{k+1}\big(I(u)\big),\ldots,\partial_{u}^{k}\phi\in H^{1}\big(I(u)\big)$ satisfy uniform bounds for $u\in[u_{0},u_{*}).$ Having established the improved estimates for the scalar field in Section 3.4, it will be straightforward to propagate the desired Sobolev norms from initial data. We notice that the uniform $H^{1}$ bound for $\phi$ follows from (3.9) and (3.21). The only nontrivial part is to establish uniform bounds for $\phi\in H^{2}\big(I(u)\big)$ and $\partial_{u}\phi\in H^{1}\big(I(u)\big)$ in (3.43). At higher order, the equations become linear in the top order quantities, so the remaining bounds follow by a propagation of regularity argument, which we do not carry out here for the sake of brevity. We also note that with respect to Bondi coordinates, the Kodama vector field takes the form $\mathcal{T}=\gamma^{-1}\partial_{u}.$ Thus, one can further show that $\phi\in H^{k+1}\big(I(u)\big),\ldots,\mathcal{T}^{k}\phi\in H^{1}\big(I(u)\big)$ satisfy uniform bounds for $u\in[u_{0},u_{*}).$

We further shrink the domain $\mathcal{D}$ by increasing $u_{0},$ so that in addition to (3.13), $r_{*}$ also satisfies:

$$ r_{*}\leq\frac{\delta^{2}\rho}{1000(1+|\Lambda|)(A+\tilde{A}+1)^{2}(1+|u_{*}-u_{0}|)}. $$

We point out that the bounds in Sections 3.2-3.4 still hold in the new domain $\mathcal{D}$ (except for (3.22) and (3.35), which are replaced by (3.23)-(3.24) and (3.36)-(3.37)).

For the rest of the proof, we establish the following bound for all $u\in[u_{0},u_{*}):$

$$ \int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(u))}r\Big[\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}+\big(\partial_{r}^{2}\phi\big)^{2}+\big(\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}+\big(\partial_{r}\phi\big)^{2}\Big](u,r)dr\leq\frac{10}{\delta}+20\int_{0}^{r_{*}}\tilde{r}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}. $$

We first commute the wave equation (3.6) with $\partial_{u}:$

$$ 2\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi+\frac{1}{r}\partial_{u}\partial_{u}\phi-\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}^{2}\partial_{u}\phi-\frac{1}{r}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi-\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi-\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}^{2}\phi-\frac{1}{r}\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\phi-\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\phi=0. $$

Multiplying this equation by $2n\partial_{u}\phi+\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi,$ we derive the energy identity:

$$ \displaystyle\partial_{r}\big(2r(n\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}\big)+n\big(r(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi)^{2}\big)= \displaystyle r\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}^{2}\phi\cdot\big[2n\partial_{u}\phi+\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big]+r\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2} \displaystyle+(\overline{\gamma}-1)\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\cdot n\partial_{u}\phi+\partial_{r}\phi\cdot\big[\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}+r\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big]\cdot\big[2n\partial_{u}\phi+\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big]. $$

We remark that the only potentially dangerous term is the first term on the RHS of (3.44), which is cubic in second derivatives of the scalar field, since $\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}$ contains a $\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\phi$ term. In our argument below, we use the improved estimates in Section 3.4 to deal with this term. We also notice that when commuting the wave equation (3.6) with more $\partial_{u}$ derivatives, we only get linear and quadratic top order terms in the corresponding energy identity, which simplifies the argument considerably.

We fix any $0<r_{1}\leq r_{*}$ and $u_{0}<u_{1}\leq u_{\Gamma}(u_{0},r_{1}).$ For any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ , we integrate the energy identity (3.44) in $\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}$ to obtain the energy estimate:

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u))}r\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}2r\big(n\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(s)\big)ds \displaystyle=\int_{0}^{r_{0}}\tilde{r}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg(r\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}^{2}\phi\cdot\big[2n\partial_{u}\phi+\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big]+\frac{1}{2}r\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle+\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\bigg((\overline{\gamma}-1)\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\cdot n\partial_{u}\phi+\partial_{r}\phi\cdot\big[\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}+r\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big]\cdot\big[2n\partial_{u}\phi+\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big]\bigg)\ d\mathrm{Vol}. $$

Motivated by (3.45), we define for any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ the energy:

$$ E^{2}(u,r_{0})=\sup\bigg\{\int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r^{\prime}}(u^{\prime}))}r\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u^{\prime},r)dr+\int_{u_{0}}^{u^{\prime}}2r\big(n\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}\big(\chi_{u_{0},r^{\prime}}(s)\big)ds:\ \chi_{u_{0},r^{\prime}}(u^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}\bigg\}. $$

Using this definition, we have for any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ :

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq|u_{*}-u_{0}|E^{2}(u,r_{0}),\ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r\big(n\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq r_{*}E^{2}(u,r_{0}). $$

Additionally, we have by (3.7) and (3.17) for any $(s,r)\in\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big|(s,r) \displaystyle=|\Lambda|r\big|\partial_{u}\gamma\big|\leq 2|\Lambda|r\gamma\int_{0}^{r}\tilde{r}\big|\partial_{r}\phi\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\phi\big|(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r} \displaystyle\leq\frac{4|\Lambda|r(A+\tilde{A})}{\delta}\int_{0}^{r}\tilde{r}^{\frac{\rho}{2}}\big|\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\phi\big|(s,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}\leq\frac{4|\Lambda|r^{1+\frac{\rho}{2}}(A+\tilde{A})}{\delta\sqrt{\rho}}E(u,r_{0}), \displaystyle\big|\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}\big|(s,r) \displaystyle\leq\frac{4|\Lambda|r^{2+\frac{\rho}{2}}(A+\tilde{A})}{\delta\sqrt{\rho}}E(u,r_{0}), $$

where we used the fact that $\partial_{u}\gamma(u,0)=\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}(u,0)=0.$

We now bound the error terms on the RHS of the energy estimate (3.45) one by one. For the second error term in (3.45), we use (3.17) and (3.46):

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}\frac{1}{2}r\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{|\Lambda|}{\delta}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r^{2}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{|\Lambda|}{\delta}|u_{*}-u_{0}|r_{*}E^{2}(u,r_{0}). $$

For the third error term in (3.45), we use (3.15) and (3.46):

$$ \iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}(\overline{\gamma}-1)\big|\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\cdot n\partial_{u}\phi\big|\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{|\Lambda|}{\delta}\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r^{2}\big|\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\cdot n\partial_{u}\phi\big|\ d\mathrm{Vol}\leq\frac{|\Lambda|}{\delta}\sqrt{|u_{*}-u_{0}|}r_{*}^{3/2}E^{2}(u,r_{0}). $$

For the fourth error term in (3.45), we use (3.36) and (3.46)-(3.48):

$$ \displaystyle\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}} \displaystyle\big|\partial_{r}\phi\big|\cdot\Big[\big|\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}\big|+r\big|\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\overline{\gamma}\big|\Big]\cdot\Big[2\big|n\partial_{u}\phi\big|+\big|\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big|\Big]\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle\leq\frac{8|\Lambda|(A+\tilde{A})^{2}}{\delta\sqrt{\rho}}E(u,r_{0})\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r^{1+\rho}\Big(2\big|n\partial_{u}\phi\big|+\big|\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big|\Big)\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle\leq\frac{32|\Lambda|(A+\tilde{A})^{2}}{\delta\sqrt{\rho}}\big(r_{*}+|u_{*}-u_{0}|\big)r_{*}^{1+\rho}E^{2}(u,r_{0}). $$

For the first error term in (3.45), we use the fact that $r|\partial_{r}^{2}\phi|\leq r^{-1/2}|\partial_{r}\psi|+2|\partial_{r}\phi|.$ The second term has just been dealt with above. For the first term we have by (3.48) and (3.37):

$$ \displaystyle\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r^{-1/2}\big|\partial_{u}\overline{\gamma}\big|\cdot\big|\partial_{r}\psi\big|\cdot\Big[2\big|n\partial_{u}\phi\big|+\big|\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big|\Big]\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle\leq\frac{4|\Lambda|(A+\tilde{A})}{\delta\sqrt{\rho}}r_{*}^{\rho/2}E(u,r_{0})\iint_{\mathcal{D}_{u,r_{0}}}r^{3/2}\big|\partial_{r}\psi\big|\Big[2\big|n\partial_{u}\phi\big|+\big|\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big|\Big]\ d\mathrm{Vol} \displaystyle\leq\frac{16|\Lambda|(A+\tilde{A})^{2}}{\delta\sqrt{\rho}}\big(r_{*}+|u_{*}-u_{0}|\big)r_{*}^{1+\rho}E^{2}(u,r_{0}). $$

Using our error term estimates in (3.45), we proved that for any $\chi_{u_{0},r_{0}}(u)\in\mathcal{D}_{u_{1},r_{1}}$ :

$$ E^{2}(u,r_{0})\leq\int_{0}^{r_{0}}\tilde{r}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}+\frac{100|\Lambda|(A+\tilde{A}+1)^{2}}{\delta\sqrt{\rho}}\big(|u_{*}-u_{0}|+1\big)r_{*}E^{2}(u,r_{0}). $$

In view of (3.42), we can absorb the error term on the LHS, so we get that for any $u\in[u_{0},u_{*}):$

$$ \int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(u))}r\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr\leq 2\int_{0}^{r_{*}}\tilde{r}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}. $$

In order to prove the uniform $H^{2}$ bound for $\phi$ , we use (3.6), (3.15), and (3.17) to get:

$$ \big|\partial_{r}^{2}\phi\big|\leq 2\big|\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\phi\big|+\frac{\big|\partial_{u}\phi-\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\phi\big|}{r}+\frac{2|\Lambda|}{\delta}r\big|\partial_{r}\phi\big|. $$

We define $\xi=\partial_{u}\phi-\overline{\gamma}\partial_{r}\phi.$ The boundary conditions at $\Gamma$ in Definition 2.6 imply that $\xi(u,0)=0.$ Moreover, we compute that $\partial_{r}(r\xi)=-r\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\phi$ . Using the Hardy inequality (3.29), we get that for any $(u,r)\in\mathcal{D}$ :

$$ \int_{0}^{r}\frac{\xi^{2}(u,\tilde{r})}{\tilde{r}}d\tilde{r}=\int_{0}^{r}\frac{(r\xi)^{2}(u,\tilde{r})}{\tilde{r}^{3}}d\tilde{r}\leq\int_{0}^{r}\frac{\big(\partial_{r}(r\xi)\big)^{2}(u,\tilde{r})}{\tilde{r}}d\tilde{r}=\int_{0}^{r}\tilde{r}\big(\partial_{u}\partial_{r}\phi\big)^{2}(u,\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}. $$

Using (3.13), (3.21), and (3.49)-(3.51), we get for any $u\in[u_{0},u_{*}):$

$$ \int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(u))}r\big(\partial_{r}^{2}\phi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr\leq 1+10\int_{0}^{r_{*}}\tilde{r}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}. $$

Finally, using (3.21), (3.49), and (3.51), we get for any $u\in[u_{0},u_{*}):$

$$ \int_{0}^{r(\chi_{u_{0},r_{*}}(u))}r\big(\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u,r)dr\leq\frac{4}{\delta}+\int_{0}^{r_{*}}\tilde{r}\big(\partial_{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)^{2}(u_{0},\tilde{r})d\tilde{r}. $$

According to (3.21), (3.49), (3.52), and (3.53), we completed the proof of (3.43). Thus, we established uniform bounds for $\phi\in H^{2}\big(I(u)\big)$ and $\partial_{u}\phi\in H^{1}\big(I(u)\big)$ . As explained previously, our argument also works for higher order derivatives, where the structure of the error terms simplifies significantly. Therefore, one can also prove uniform bounds for $\phi\in H^{k+1}\big(I(u)\big),\ldots,\partial_{u}^{k}\phi\in H^{1}\big(I(u)\big),$ which contradicts Assumption 3.1, completing the proof of Theorem 1.2. ∎

## 4 Trapped surface formation criterion

We prove a criterion for trapped surface formation following the strategy of Christodoulou in [12]. We recall the statement of Theorem 1.3: See 1.3

#### Proof.

Throughout the proof we use the indices $1$ and $2$ for quantities evaluated on $C_{1}$ respectively $C_{2}.$ We first claim that there exists $u_{0}<u_{1}<0$ such that $r_{2}(u_{1})=\frac{5\delta_{0}/4}{1+\delta_{0}}r_{2}(u_{0}).$ Supposing this is not true, we have by Section 2.4 that $\overline{C_{2}}\cap\mathcal{B}_{0}\neq\emptyset$ (since $r=0$ on $\mathcal{B}$ and $C_{1}\cap\Gamma=\emptyset$ ). By equation (2.3), we have that for any $u_{0}<u<0:$

$$ \frac{5\delta_{0}/4}{1+\delta_{0}}r_{2}(u_{0})<r_{2}(u)\leq r_{1}(u)+\delta_{0}r_{1}(u_{0}). $$

Taking $u\rightarrow 0^{-},$ we obtain the contradiction $r_{2}(u_{0})<r_{1}(u_{0}).$

We fix $u_{0}<u_{1}<0$ such that $r_{2}(u_{1})=\frac{5\delta_{0}/4}{1+\delta_{0}}r_{2}(u_{0})$ . We assume the conclusion is false, so there exist no marginally trapped surfaces on $C_{2}$ for $u\in[u_{0},u_{1}].$ At first, we also assume that $m_{2}(u)-m_{1}(u)>0$ for all $u\in[u_{0},u_{1}]$ .

A key role in the proof is played by the quantity $\eta:=|\Lambda|^{-1}r_{2}^{-2}(m_{2}-m_{1}),$ for which we aim to derive a differential inequality. Using equation (2.9), we compute for any $u\in[u_{0},u_{1}]$ :

$$ \partial_{u}\big(m_{2}-m_{1}\big)=-\frac{4}{\gamma_{2}}\cdot\bigg(r_{2}\big(\partial_{u}\phi_{2}\big)^{2}-\frac{\gamma_{2}}{\gamma_{1}}r_{1}\big(\partial_{u}\phi_{1}\big)^{2}\bigg)=-\frac{4}{\gamma_{2}}\cdot\bigg(\zeta^{2}+2\zeta\sqrt{r_{1}}\partial_{u}\phi_{1}-\bigg(\frac{\gamma_{2}}{\gamma_{1}}-1\bigg)r_{1}\big(\partial_{u}\phi_{1}\big)^{2}\bigg), $$

where we denoted $\zeta=\sqrt{r_{2}}\partial_{u}\phi_{2}-\sqrt{r_{1}}\partial_{u}\phi_{1}.$ By the assumption $m_{2}(u)-m_{1}(u)>0$ , equations (2.8) and (2.12) imply $\gamma_{2}>\gamma_{1}.$ We further get:

$$ \partial_{u}\big(m_{2}-m_{1}\big)\geq-\frac{4}{\gamma_{2}}\cdot\bigg(1+\frac{1}{\gamma_{2}/\gamma_{1}-1}\bigg)\zeta^{2}\geq-\frac{4}{\gamma_{2}}\cdot\bigg(1+\frac{1}{\log(\gamma_{2}/\gamma_{1})}\bigg)\zeta^{2}. $$

Using $m\geq 1$ and the equations (2.12), (2.8), (2.2), we have the bounds for any $u\in[u_{0},u_{1}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\log\frac{\gamma_{2}}{\gamma_{1}} \displaystyle=\int_{v_{1}}^{v_{2}}r\frac{(\partial_{v}\phi)^{2}}{\partial_{v}r}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}=\int_{v_{1}}^{v_{2}}\frac{\partial_{v}m}{-4\Omega^{-2}\partial_{u}r\partial_{v}r}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\geq\frac{m_{2}-m_{1}}{|\Lambda|r_{2}^{2}}=\eta>0, \displaystyle\zeta^{2} \displaystyle\leq\bigg(\int_{v_{1}}^{v_{2}}\frac{|\partial_{u}r|\cdot|\partial_{v}\phi|}{2\sqrt{r}}\bigg)^{2}\leq\big(m_{2}-m_{1}\big)\int_{v_{1}}^{v_{2}}\frac{\Omega^{2}|\partial_{u}r|}{16r^{2}}\leq\frac{(m_{2}-m_{1})\cdot\gamma_{2}\cdot|\partial_{u}r_{2}|}{16r_{2}}\bigg(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}-1\bigg). $$

We use (4.2)-(4.3) in (4.1):

$$ \partial_{u}\big(m_{2}-m_{1}\big)\geq-\frac{(m_{2}-m_{1})\cdot|\partial_{u}r_{2}|}{4r_{2}}\bigg(1+\frac{1}{\eta}\bigg)\cdot\bigg(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}-1\bigg). $$

Using the fact that $\eta=|\Lambda|^{-1}r_{2}^{-2}(m_{2}-m_{1}),$ we can rewrite this bound for any $u\in[u_{0},u_{1}]$ :

$$ \partial_{u}\eta\geq\eta\cdot\frac{|\partial_{u}r_{2}|}{4r_{2}}\cdot\bigg[8-\bigg(1+\frac{1}{\eta}\bigg)\cdot\bigg(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}-1\bigg)\bigg]. $$

We introduce the variable $x=r_{2}(u)/r_{2}(u_{0})$ along $C_{2},$ and we notice that (2.3) implies:

$$ \frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}-1\leq\frac{\delta_{0}}{x(1+\delta_{0})-\delta_{0}}. $$

We rewrite inequality (4.4) for any $x\in\big[\frac{5\delta_{0}/4}{1+\delta_{0}},1\big]$ :

$$ -x\partial_{x}\eta\geq\eta\bigg[2-\frac{1}{4}\frac{\delta_{0}}{x(1+\delta_{0})-\delta_{0}}\bigg(1+\frac{1}{\eta}\bigg)\bigg]=\mathbf{g}\eta-\mathbf{f}, $$

$$ \mathbf{f}=\frac{1}{4}\frac{\delta_{0}}{x(1+\delta_{0})-\delta_{0}},\ \mathbf{g}=2-\mathbf{f}. $$

We integrate to get that for any $x\in\big[\frac{5\delta_{0}/4}{1+\delta_{0}},1\big]$ :

$$ \eta_{0}\leq\mathbf{F}(x)+\eta(x)e^{-\mathbf{G}(x)}, $$

$$ \mathbf{F}(x)=\int_{x}^{1}e^{-\mathbf{G}(x^{\prime})}f(x^{\prime})\frac{dx^{\prime}}{x^{\prime}},\ \mathbf{G}(x)=\int_{x}^{1}g(x^{\prime})\frac{dx^{\prime}}{x^{\prime}}. $$

By assumption, the circle $(u_{1},v_{2})$ is not trapped, so for $x_{1}:=r_{2}(u_{1})/r_{2}(u_{0}):$

$$ \eta(x_{1})=\frac{m_{2}(u_{1})-m_{1}(u_{1})}{|\Lambda|r_{2}^{2}(u_{1})}\leq\frac{m_{2}(u_{1})-1}{|\Lambda|r_{2}^{2}(u_{1})}\leq 1, $$

which implies that $\eta_{0}\leq\mathbf{F}(x_{1})+e^{-\mathbf{G}(x_{1})}.$ We recall that we chose $u_{1}$ such that $x_{1}=\frac{5\delta_{0}/4}{1+\delta_{0}}.$ While not essential to the proof, we remark that the minimum of $\mathbf{F}(x)+e^{-\mathbf{G}(x)}$ for $x\in\big[\frac{5\delta_{0}/4}{1+\delta_{0}},1\big]$ is attained exactly at $x_{1},$ where we have that $\mathbf{f}(x_{1})=\mathbf{g}(x_{1})=1.$ Finally, we compute that:

$$ e^{-\mathbf{G}(x)}=x^{2}\bigg(\frac{x}{x(1+\delta_{0})-\delta_{0}}\bigg)^{1/4},\ \mathbf{F}(x)=\frac{\delta_{0}}{4}\int_{x}^{1}\bigg(\frac{x^{\prime}}{x^{\prime}(1+\delta_{0})-\delta_{0}}\bigg)^{5/4}dx^{\prime}, $$

$$ \eta_{0}\leq\mathbf{F}(x_{1})+e^{-\mathbf{G}(x_{1})}=\frac{\delta_{0}}{4}+O\big(\delta_{0}^{2}|\log\delta_{0}|\big). $$

However, we have that $\eta_{0}>\delta_{0},$ which leads to a contradiction for $\delta_{0}>0$ small enough.

We recall that in the above proof we assumed that for all $u\in[u_{0},u_{1}]$ , we have $m_{2}(u)-m_{1}(u)>0$ . To deal with the remaining case, we denote $u_{*}=\inf_{[u_{0},u_{1}]}\{u:\ m_{2}(u)=m_{1}(u)\},$ and we have that $u_{*}\in(u_{0},u_{1}].$ We can repeat the above proof on the interval $[u_{0},u_{*})$ instead of $[u_{0},u_{1}).$ We denote $x_{*}:=r_{2}(u_{*})/r_{2}(u_{0}),$ and we get that $\eta_{0}\leq\mathbf{F}(x_{*})+\eta(x_{*})e^{-\mathbf{G}(x_{*})}=\mathbf{F}(x_{*})$ , since $m_{2}(u_{*})=m_{1}(u_{*})$ . However, we have $\mathbf{F}(x)<\delta_{0}/2$ for all $x\in[x_{1},1],$ which again contradicts $\eta_{0}>\delta_{0}.$ ∎

## 5 Locally naked singularity spacetimes

In this section, we provide a detailed description of locally naked singularity spacetimes in a neighborhood of the first singularity at the center. Throughout this section, we fix $k\geq 2$ and we consider $\big(\mathcal{M},g,\phi\big)$ to be the maximal globally hyperbolic development of a $C^{k}$ characteristic data set $\mathfrak{D}$ on the outgoing null cone $C_{0}^{+}.$ We assume that $b_{\Gamma}$ is a first singularity at the center $\Gamma$ and that the ingoing null cone $C_{0}^{-}$ passing through $b_{\Gamma}$ intersects $C_{0}^{+}$ (rather than $\mathcal{I}$ ). We choose double null coordinates $(u,v)$ such that:

$$ b_{\Gamma}=(0,0),\ C_{0}^{-}=\big\{v=0,\ 2r=-u\big\},\ C_{0}^{+}=\big\{u=u_{0},\ 2r=v-u_{0}\big\}. $$

Moreover, we assume that $\big(\mathcal{M},g\big)$ is a locally naked singularity spacetime, as defined in (2.41), so $\mathcal{B}_{0}\neq\emptyset.$ In particular, according to Section 2.4, there exists $v_{1}>0$ such that $[u_{0},0)\times[0,v_{1}]\subset\mathcal{R}$ .

As a consequence of Theorem 1.2 and Lemma 2.2, we have that for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},0)\times[0,v_{1}]:$

$$ 1\leq m(u,v)\leq 1+|\Lambda|r^{2}(u,v). $$

This further implies a lower bound for $\gamma$ on $C_{0}^{-}$ :

$$ \gamma(u,0)=\frac{-4\partial_{u}r(u,0)}{|\Lambda|r^{2}(u,0)+1-m(u,0)}\geq 8|\Lambda|^{-1}|u|^{-2}. $$

Moreover, we notice that (2.5) implies that $\partial_{u}\Omega^{-2}\geq 0,$ so $\Omega^{2}$ is decreasing along $C_{0}^{-}$ .

Next, we introduce the blueshift, which plays an essential role in our analysis:

#### Definition 5.1.

We define the blueshift as the function $\mathbf{b}:[u_{0},0)\times[0,v_{1}]\rightarrow[0,\infty):$

$$ \mathbf{b}(u,v)=\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\frac{|\Lambda|}{2}r\gamma(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}. $$

We denote $\mathbf{b}(u)=\mathbf{b}(u,0).$ We also define the function $\mathbf{s}:[u_{0},0)\rightarrow[0,\infty):$

$$ \mathbf{s}(u)=\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\frac{|\Lambda|}{4}r^{2}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)du^{\prime}. $$

Using this notation, we can integrate (2.3) to obtain that:

$$ \partial_{v}r(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u,v)}. $$

In particular, we have $e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\gamma(u,0)=2\partial_{v}r(u,0)\gamma(u,0)=2\Omega^{2}(u,0)\leq 2\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$ We use this bound for the rest of the section without explicit reference.

We prove that all first singularities at the center have unbounded blueshift on $C_{0}^{-}$ :

#### Proposition 5.1.

The blueshift $\mathbf{b}:[u_{0},0)\rightarrow[0,\infty)$ is unbounded on $C_{0}^{-}$ and satisfies the quantitative estimate:

$$ \mathbf{b}(u)\geq 2\log\frac{u_{0}}{u}. $$

The lower bound (5.6) holds more generally for any solution $\big(\mathcal{M},g,\phi\big)$ with a first singularity $b_{\Gamma}\in\overline{\Gamma}\backslash\Gamma$ (which is not necessarily locally naked).

#### Proof.

The proof is immediate by using (5.2) and (5.3). We note this only relies on (5.1) on $C_{0}^{-},$ which indeed holds for any first singularity at the center, without assuming that the solution is a locally naked singularity spacetime. ∎

In order to state our next result, we introduce notation similar to that of Section 4. For any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},0)\times[0,v_{1}],$ we define:

$$ \eta(u,v)=\frac{m(u,v)-m(u,0)}{|\Lambda|r^{2}(u,v)},\ \delta(u,v)=\frac{r(u,v)}{r(u,0)}-1. $$

We make the notation convention for the rest of this section that we write $x\lesssim y$ for any quantities $x,y>0$ if there is a constant $C\big(k,|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)\big)>0$ such that $x\leq Cy.$

We prove further a priori bounds for the solution $\big(\mathcal{M},g,\phi\big):$

#### Proposition 5.2.

For any $\epsilon>0$ sufficiently small depending on $|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)$ , and any $v_{0}\in(0,v_{1})$ sufficiently small depending on $\epsilon,|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0),\gamma|_{C_{0}^{+}\cap\{0\leq v\leq v_{1}\}},$ we define the region:

$$ \mathcal{P}=\Big\{(u,v)\in[u_{0},0)\times[0,v_{0}]:\ v^{1/2}\mathbf{s}(u)\leq\epsilon\Big\}, $$

represented schematically in Figure 2. Then, for any $(u,v)\in\mathcal{P}$ we have that:

$$ \eta(u,v)\leq\delta(u,v), $$

$$ \partial_{v}r(u,v)\leq 100e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}, $$

$$ \gamma(u,0)\leq\gamma(u,v)\leq 100\gamma(u,0), $$

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq 10^{4}|\Lambda|\cdot v|u|e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\gamma(u,0), $$

$$ \int_{u}^{0}|u^{\prime}|\gamma^{-1}(u^{\prime},0)\cdot\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{P}}(u^{\prime},v)\big|\partial_{u}\phi\big|^{2}(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}\lesssim|u|^{2}, $$

where $\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{P}}$ represents the characteristic function of $\mathcal{P}.$

#### Proof.

We notice that $\mathbf{s}$ is increasing, so if $(\tilde{u},\tilde{v})\in\mathcal{P}$ then $[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]\subset\mathcal{P}.$ We make the following bootstrap assumptions for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]\subset\mathcal{P}$ :

$$ \partial_{v}r(u,v)\leq 100e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}, $$

$$ \gamma(u,v)\leq 100\gamma(u,0). $$

We first check that (5.13)-(5.14) hold initially with significantly better constants. In view of (5.5) and $2r(u_{0},v)=v-u_{0},$ we have for $(u,v)\in\big(C_{0}^{-}\cup C_{0}^{+}\big)\cap\mathcal{P}$ that $\partial_{v}r(u,v)\leq e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}.$ By continuity, we have that $\gamma(u_{0},v)\leq 2\gamma(u_{0},0)$ for all $v\in[0,v_{0}],$ where $v_{0}>0$ is small enough depending on $\gamma|_{C_{0}^{+}\cap\{0\leq v\leq v_{1}\}}$ .

Next, we have by (5.13), (5.6) for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \delta(u,v)=\frac{\int_{0}^{v}\partial_{v}r(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}}{r(u,0)}\leq\frac{200e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}v}{|u|}\leq\frac{200|u|v}{|u_{0}|^{2}}. $$

For $v_{0}$ sufficiently small in terms of $|u_{0}|,$ we have for all $v\in(0,v_{0}]$ that $\delta(u,v)$ is small enough, as in the statement of Theorem 1.3. Since $[u_{0},0)\times[0,v_{0}]\subset\mathcal{R},$ Theorem 1.3 implies that $\eta(u,v)\leq\delta(u,v)$ for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ .

We prove some preliminary estimates for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ . By monotonicity, we have that $r\geq|u|/2,\ \partial_{u}r\leq-1/2,$ and $\gamma(u,v)\geq\gamma(u,0).$ Also, for $v_{0}$ sufficiently small in terms of $|u_{0}|,$ we have that (5.13) and (5.6) imply $r\leq|u|.$ Moreover, we have by (2.3), (5.5), (5.13), and (5.14):

$$ \displaystyle|\partial_{u}r| \displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{2}+\int_{0}^{v}|\Lambda|\cdot|u|\gamma(u,v^{\prime})\partial_{v}r(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq\frac{1}{2}+10^{4}|\Lambda|\cdot v|u|e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\gamma(u,0) \displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{2}+2\cdot 10^{4}|\Lambda|\cdot v|u|\Omega^{2}(u,0)\leq\frac{1}{2}+2\cdot 10^{4}|\Lambda|\cdot v|u_{0}|\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)<1, $$

for $v_{0}$ sufficiently small in terms of $|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$

We now improve the bootstrap assumptions. Since $\eta(u,v)\leq\delta(u,v),$ we get by (2.8), (2.12), (5.5), (5.14), and (5.15) that for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\log\frac{\gamma(u,v)}{\gamma(u,0)} \displaystyle=\int_{0}^{v}\frac{r(\partial_{v}\phi)^{2}}{\partial_{v}r}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}=\int_{0}^{v}\frac{\gamma\partial_{v}m}{-4\partial_{u}r}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq 50|\Lambda|\gamma(u,0)|u|^{2}\eta(u,v) \displaystyle\leq 50|\Lambda|\gamma(u,0)|u|^{2}\delta(u,v)\leq 10^{4}|\Lambda|\cdot v|u|e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\gamma(u,0)\leq 2\cdot 10^{4}|\Lambda|\cdot v|u_{0}|\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)<1, $$

for $v_{0}$ sufficiently small in terms of $|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$ Thus, we improved the bootstrap assumption (5.14). We notice that in the above we also proved that for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}=\int_{0}^{v}\frac{r(\partial_{v}\phi)^{2}}{\partial_{v}r}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq 10^{4}|\Lambda|\cdot v|u|e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\gamma(u,0). $$

Using (2.12), (5.5), (5.13), (5.14), and (5.17), we have the following estimate for the blueshift for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle|\mathbf{b} \displaystyle(u,v)-\mathbf{b}(u)|\lesssim\int_{0}^{v}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\partial_{v}(r\gamma)(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})du^{\prime}dv^{\prime}\lesssim\int_{0}^{v}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\Big(\gamma\partial_{v}r+|u^{\prime}|\gamma\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r\Big)(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})du^{\prime}dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim v\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|\gamma(u^{\prime},0)\bigg(\int_{0}^{v}\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\bigg)du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim v|u_{0}|\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)+v\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{2}\gamma^{2}(u^{\prime},0)e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\lesssim v|u_{0}|\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)+v\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)\cdot\mathbf{s}(u)\lesssim\epsilon, $$

for $v_{0}$ sufficiently small in terms of $\epsilon,|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$ We use this estimate in (5.5):

$$ \partial_{v}r(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u,v)}=\frac{1}{2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\big(1+O(\epsilon)\big)\leq 10e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}, $$

provided that $\epsilon>0$ is sufficiently small in terms of $|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$ This allows us to improve the assumption (5.13) as well.

We improved the bootstrap assumptions (5.13)-(5.14), so we proved (5.8)-(5.11) for all $(u,v)\in\mathcal{P}.$ As a consequence of (5.1), we have that for any $u_{0}\leq u_{1}<u_{2}<0$ and $v\in[0,v_{1}]:$

$$ 0\leq m(u_{1},v)-m(u_{2},v)\leq|\Lambda|r^{2}(u_{1},v). $$

Using this inequality, together with (2.9) and the bounds established in $\mathcal{P}$ completes the proof of (5.12). ∎

#### Remark 5.1.

The function $\mathbf{s}(u)$ can be interpreted as a measurement for the strength of the blueshift, which affects the size of the region $\mathcal{P}.$ In the case when $\mathbf{s}(u)$ is bounded, we can take $\mathcal{P}=[u_{0},0)\times[0,v_{0}]$ and we obtain a priori estimates all the way to $\mathcal{B}_{0}.$ In particular, (1.21) implies this is the case for the examples of locally naked singularities constructed in [19].

## 6 Instability to trapped surface formation

In this section, we prove that all locally naked singularity spacetimes are unstable to trapped surface formation arbitrarily close to $b_{\Gamma}$ . Let $\big(\mathcal{M},g,\phi\big)$ be a locally naked singularity spacetime satisfying the set-up in Section 5. In particular, $\big(\mathcal{M},g,\phi\big)$ is the maximal globally hyperbolic development of a $C^{k}$ characteristic data set $\mathfrak{D}$ , for some $k\geq 2$ . We also assume that the ingoing null cone $C_{0}^{-}$ passing through $b_{\Gamma}$ intersects $C_{0}^{+}$ , and we choose double null coordinates $(u,v)$ such that:

$$ b_{\Gamma}=(0,0),\ C_{0}^{-}=\big\{v=0,\ 2r=-u\big\},\ C_{0}^{+}=\big\{u=u_{0},\ 2r=v-u_{0}\big\}. $$

Moreover, we take $v_{1}>0$ such that $[u_{0},0)\times[0,v_{1}]\subset\mathcal{R}$ , and we fix $v_{0},\epsilon>0$ as required in Section 5.

We fix any integer $n>k+1$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$ . We define characteristic data on $\big\{u=u_{0},\ v\in[u_{0},v_{1}]\big\}:$

$$ r_{\lambda}=r,\ \phi_{\lambda}=\phi,\ \Omega_{\lambda}=\Omega\ \text{on }\big\{u=u_{0},\ v\in[u_{0},0]\big\},\ r_{\lambda}=r,\ \theta_{\lambda}=\theta+\lambda v^{n}\ \text{on }\big\{u=u_{0},\ v\in[0,v_{1}]\big\}, $$

where $\phi_{\lambda}$ and $\Omega_{\lambda}$ are defined on $\big\{u=u_{0},\ v\in(0,v_{1}]\big\}$ according to (2.10) and (2.6). Since $n>k+1,$ the characteristic data $\big(r_{\lambda},\Omega_{\lambda},\phi_{\lambda}\big)$ determines uniquely a $C^{k}$ characteristic partial data set $\mathfrak{D}_{\lambda}$ , as in Definition A.1, which coincides with $\mathfrak{D}$ for $\big\{u=u_{0},\ v\in[u_{0},0]\big\}.$

We denote by $\big(\mathcal{M}_{\lambda},g_{\lambda},\phi_{\lambda}\big)$ the maximal globally hyperbolic development of the $C^{k}$ characteristic partial data set $\mathfrak{D}_{\lambda}$ . By domain of dependence, we have that $r_{\lambda}=r,\ \phi_{\lambda}=\phi,\ \Omega_{\lambda}=\Omega$ for $v\leq 0.$ The main result of this section is the instability of locally naked singularity spacetimes to trapped surface formation:

#### Proposition 6.1.

For any $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\},$ the spacetime $\big(\mathcal{M}_{\lambda},g_{\lambda}\big)$ contains a sequence of trapped surfaces converging to $b_{\Gamma}.$

The proof of Proposition 6.1 consists of two parts. First, in Section 6.1 we prove existence of the solution $\big(\mathcal{M}_{\lambda},g_{\lambda},\phi_{\lambda}\big)$ and quantitative bounds in a suitable region $\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}.$ A key aspect is that the estimates proved are consistent with the fact that the initial data perturbation in (6.1) vanishes to order $n$ at $C_{0}^{-}.$ Second, in Section 6.2 we define a curve $\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}$ which converges to $b_{\Gamma}$ and is contained in $\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}$ sufficiently close to $b_{\Gamma}$ . We prove that the blueshift effect causes the amplification of $\theta_{\lambda}$ on $\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}$ , with the main term coming from the $\lambda v^{n}$ perturbation in (6.1). We can then apply the formation of trapped surfaces criterion in Theorem 1.3 for symmetry circles on $\mathcal{C}_{\lambda}$ to complete the proof of Proposition 6.1.

### 6.1 Estimates for the perturbed spacetime

The main result of this section establishes existence and quantitative estimates in the region $\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}:$

#### Proposition 6.2.

For any $\epsilon^{\prime}\in(0,\epsilon)$ sufficiently small depending on $\lambda,n,|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)$ , and any $v_{0}^{\prime}\in(0,v_{0})$ sufficiently small depending on $\lambda,n,\epsilon^{\prime},|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0),\gamma|_{C_{0}^{+}\cap\{0\leq v\leq v_{1}\}},$ we define the region:

$$ \mathcal{P}_{\lambda}=\bigg\{u\in[u_{0},0),\ 0\leq v\leq\min\big(v_{0}^{\prime},\lambda^{4},|u|^{\frac{1}{n}}\big),\ |\lambda|v^{n+\frac{1}{4}}\leq e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{10n}}\sqrt{\gamma(u,0)},\ v^{\frac{1}{10n}}\mathbf{s}(u)\leq\epsilon^{\prime}\bigg\}, $$

represented schematically in Figure 3. The solution $\big(\mathcal{M}_{\lambda},g_{\lambda},\phi_{\lambda}\big)$ exists and satisfies the quantitative bounds in the region $\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}$ :

$$ \partial_{v}r_{\lambda}(u,v)\leq 10e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}, $$

$$ \big|\gamma_{\lambda}(u,v)-\gamma(u,0)\big|\leq 100e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}v^{1/4}|u|\gamma^{2}(u,0), $$

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\big|\theta_{\lambda}-\theta\big|^{2}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq 100\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\Big|\big(\theta_{\lambda}-\theta\big)(u,v^{\prime})-e^{\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u,v^{\prime})}\big(\theta_{\lambda}-\theta\big)(u_{0},v^{\prime})\Big|^{2}dv^{\prime}\leq\lambda^{2}v^{2n+\frac{4}{3}}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

We prove Proposition 6.2 for the rest of Section 6.1. We recall that along $C_{0}^{-}$ we have that $\mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{s}$ are increasing, while $\Omega^{2}$ is decreasing. Thus, if $(\tilde{u},\tilde{v})\in\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}$ then $[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]\subset\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}.$ We make the bootstrap assumptions in for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]\subset\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}$ :

$$ \partial_{v}r_{\lambda}(u,v)\leq 10e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}, $$

$$ \big|\gamma_{\lambda}(u,v)-\gamma(u,0)\big|\leq 100e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}v^{1/4}|u|\gamma^{2}(u,0), $$

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\big|\theta_{\lambda}-\theta\big|^{2}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq 100\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

We first check that (6.7)-(6.9) hold initially with significantly better constants. By (5.5) and (6.1), we have that $\partial_{v}r_{\lambda}(u,v)=\partial_{v}r(u,v)\leq e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}$ for any $(u,v)\in\big(C_{0}^{-}\cup C_{0}^{+}\big)\cap\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}.$ Moreover, (6.1) also implies:

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\big|\theta_{\lambda}-\theta\big|^{2}(u_{0},v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}=\frac{\lambda^{2}}{2n+1}v^{2n+1}\leq\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u_{0})}. $$

Next, we have by (2.12), (6.1), (6.2), and the proof of Proposition 5.2 that for any $(u_{0},v)\in C_{0}^{+}\cap\mathcal{P}_{\lambda}:$

$$ \displaystyle 0\leq\frac{\gamma_{\lambda}(u_{0},v)}{\gamma(u_{0},0)}-1 \displaystyle\leq 2\int_{0}^{v}\theta^{2}_{\lambda}\partial_{v}r_{\lambda}(u_{0},v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq 4\int_{0}^{v}\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r(u_{0},v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}+\frac{2\lambda^{2}}{2n+1}v^{2n+1} \displaystyle\leq 4|\Lambda|\gamma(u_{0},0)\cdot v|u_{0}|+\gamma(u_{0},0)\cdot v^{\frac{1}{2}}|u_{0}|^{1+\frac{1}{5n}}\leq e^{-\mathbf{b}(u_{0})}v^{1/4}|u_{0}|\gamma(u_{0},0), $$

for $v_{0}^{\prime}$ sufficiently small in terms of $|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$

In order to prove Proposition 6.2, it suffices to improve the bootstrap assumptions (6.7)-(6.9) in $[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ . In Section 6.1.1 we improve the bootstrap assumptions (6.7)-(6.8). The most difficult part of the proof is improving (6.9). In particular, we point out that in (6.9) we need to capture the same order of vanishing as on the initial data in (6.10). We establish further estimates for the solution in Section 6.1.2. We then improve the bootstrap assumption (6.9) in Section 6.1.3, completing the proof of Proposition 6.2.

We make the notation convention for the rest of this section that we write $x\lesssim y$ for any quantities $x,y>0$ if there is a constant $C\big(k,n,|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)\big)>0$ such that $x\leq Cy.$ Additionally, for any quantity $\psi$ we denote $\widetilde{\psi}=\psi_{\lambda}-\psi.$

#### 6.1.1 Improving the bootstrap assumptions (6.7)-(6.8)

We begin the proof of Proposition 6.2 by improving the bootstrap assumptions (6.7)-(6.8). Firstly, (6.7) implies that for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]:$

$$ \big|r_{\lambda}(u,v)-r(u,0)\big|\leq 10ve^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

As a result, $|u|/2\leq r_{\lambda}(u,v)\leq|u|.$ By taking $v_{0}^{\prime}$ sufficiently small in terms of $|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0),$ the bootstrap assumption (6.8) implies that $\gamma(u,0)\leq\gamma_{\lambda}(u,v)\leq 2\gamma(u,0).$ Similarly to the proof of (5.16), the bootstrap assumption (6.7) also implies that $1/2\leq|\partial_{u}r_{\lambda}|\leq 1,$ provided that $v_{0}^{\prime}$ is sufficiently small in terms of $|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$ We use these bounds for $r_{\lambda},\gamma_{\lambda},\partial_{u}r_{\lambda}$ for the rest of the proof without explicit reference.

According to (5.11),(5.18), (6.7), and (6.9):

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{v}\theta_{\lambda}^{2}\partial_{v}r_{\lambda}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\leq 20e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\int_{0}^{v}\big|\theta_{\lambda}-\theta\big|^{2}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}+20e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\int_{0}^{v}\theta^{2}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\leq 10^{4}\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}+100\int_{0}^{v}\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\leq 10^{4}\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}+10^{6}|\Lambda|\cdot v|u|e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\gamma(u,0)\leq e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}v^{\frac{1}{3}}|u|\gamma(u,0), $$

for $v_{0}^{\prime}$ sufficiently small in terms of $|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$ We note that in the derivation of (6.11) we used the fact that (6.2) implies $\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}\leq v^{\frac{1}{2}}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|\cdot|u_{0}|^{\frac{1}{5n}}\gamma(u,0).$

The RHS of (6.11) is bounded by $2v^{\frac{1}{3}}|u_{0}|\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0),$ so it is small. Thus, (2.12) and (6.11) imply:

$$ \big|\gamma_{\lambda}(u,v)-\gamma(u,0)\big|\leq 2\gamma(u,0)\int_{0}^{v}\theta_{\lambda}^{2}\partial_{v}r_{\lambda}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\leq e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}v^{\frac{1}{4}}|u|\gamma^{2}(u,0), $$

improving the bootstrap assumptions (6.8).

Next, we estimate the blueshift difference using a similar argument to Proposition 5.2. Using (2.12), (5.5), (6.7), and (6.11), we have for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle|\mathbf{b}_{\lambda} \displaystyle(u,v)-\mathbf{b}(u)|\lesssim\int_{0}^{v}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\Big(\gamma_{\lambda}\partial_{v}r_{\lambda}+|u^{\prime}|\gamma_{\lambda}\theta_{\lambda}^{2}\partial_{v}r_{\lambda}\Big)(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})du^{\prime}dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim v\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|\gamma(u^{\prime},0)\bigg(\int_{0}^{v}\theta_{\lambda}^{2}\partial_{v}r_{\lambda}(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\bigg)du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim v|u_{0}|\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)+v^{\frac{1}{3}}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{2}\gamma^{2}(u^{\prime},0)e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\lesssim v|u_{0}|\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)+v^{\frac{1}{3}}\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)\cdot\mathbf{s}(u). $$

Thus, by (6.2) we have for $v_{0}^{\prime}$ sufficiently small in terms of $n,|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0):$

$$ |\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u,v)-\mathbf{b}(u)|\leq v^{\frac{1}{4}}. $$

As a result, we have that for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \partial_{v}r_{\lambda}(u,v)=\frac{1}{2}e^{-\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u,v)}=\frac{1}{2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\big(1+O(v^{\frac{1}{4}})\big), $$

which improves the bootstrap assumption (6.7).

#### 6.1.2 Refined estimates

The final step in the proof of Proposition 6.2 is to improve the bootstrap assumption (6.9). For this we first need to establish more precise bounds which capture higher order vanishing properties at $v=0.$ We also recall that we are using the notation $\widetilde{\psi}=\psi_{\lambda}-\psi.$

#### Lemma 6.1.

Under the bootstrap assumptions (6.7)-(6.9), the following bounds hold for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{\gamma}\big|(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle ve^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|\gamma^{2}(u,0)\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\gamma(u,0)\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}\gamma(u,0)e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}, \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n+1}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\mathbf{x}(u)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}, \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{r}\big|(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}v\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n+1}+|\lambda|v^{n+2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\mathbf{x}(u)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}, \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{\partial_{u}r}\big|(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle v|u|\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)/2}|u|^{1/2}\gamma(u,0)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}\gamma(u,0), \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{\sqrt{r}\partial_{u}\phi}\big|(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle v|u|^{-1/2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\sqrt{\gamma(u,0)}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|\lambda|\cdot|u|^{-1}v^{n+1}, $$

where we use the notation:

$$ \mathbf{x}(u)=\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\big(|u^{\prime}|\gamma(u^{\prime},0)\big)^{3/2}du^{\prime}. $$

#### Proof.

We notice that we have the inequality:

$$ \big|\widetilde{\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r}\big|\lesssim\theta^{2}\big|\widetilde{\partial_{v}r}\big|+e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|\theta|\cdot\big|\widetilde{\theta}\big|+e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\big|\widetilde{\theta}\big|^{2}. $$

We integrate this inequality, and use (5.11), (5.18), (6.13) for the first term, (5.11), (6.9) for the second term, and (6.9) for the third term. Thus, we get that for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{v}\big|\widetilde{\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim v|u|\gamma(u,0)\sup_{v^{\prime}\in[0,v]}\big|\widetilde{\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v^{\prime})+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)} \displaystyle\lesssim v|u|\gamma(u,0)e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

According to (6.2), the RHS of (6.19) is bounded up to a constant by $v^{\frac{1}{2}}|u_{0}|^{1+\frac{1}{5n}}\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0),$ so it is small for $v_{0}^{\prime}$ sufficiently small in terms of $|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$ As a result, (2.12) implies that:

$$ \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{\gamma}\big|(u,v) \displaystyle\lesssim\gamma(u,v)\cdot\int_{0}^{v}\big|\widetilde{\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim v|u|\gamma^{2}(u,0)e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\gamma(u,0)\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}\gamma(u,0)e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

By induction we prove that for any $0\leq i\leq n$ and $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{\gamma}\big|(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle ve^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|\gamma^{2}(u,0)\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{i}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\gamma(u,0)\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}\gamma(u,0)e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}, \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{i}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\mathbf{x}(u)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}. $$

According to (5.18), (6.13), and (6.20), we already established the case $i=0$ . We assume the induction hypothesis holds for $0\leq i\leq n-1$ and prove it for $i+1.$ We first have the preliminary estimate:

$$ \big|\widetilde{r}\big|(u,v)\lesssim e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}v\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{i}+|\lambda|v^{n+2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\mathbf{x}(u)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}. $$

As a result, we get by combining (6.21) with (6.23) and using (5.2) that for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{r\gamma}\big|(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle ve^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{2}\gamma^{2}(u,0)\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{i}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\big(|u|\gamma(u,0)\big)^{3/2}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}|u|\gamma(u,0)e^{\mathbf{b}(u)} \displaystyle+|\lambda|\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)v^{n+2}\mathbf{x}(u)+\lambda^{2}\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0)v^{2n+2}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

We notice that by Definition 5.1, we have that:

$$ \int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|\gamma(u^{\prime},0)e^{\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\lesssim e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

We integrate (6.24), using (6.25) and the fact that $\mathbf{s},\mathbf{x}$ are non-decreasing to get that:

$$ \int_{u_{0}}^{u}\big|\widetilde{r\gamma}\big|(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}\lesssim\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{i+1}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\mathbf{x}(u)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

We bound the last two terms on the RHS of (6.26) using (6.2):

$$ \displaystyle|\lambda|v^{n+1}\mathbf{x}(u) \displaystyle\lesssim\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{\frac{3}{2}}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)\cdot v^{\frac{3}{4}}|u^{\prime}|^{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{10n}}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)du^{\prime}\lesssim|u_{0}|^{\frac{1}{10n}}v^{\frac{3}{4}}\mathbf{s}(u), \displaystyle\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)} \displaystyle\lesssim v^{\frac{1}{2}}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{1+\frac{1}{5n}}\gamma(u,0)\lesssim|u_{0}|^{1+\frac{1}{5n}}v^{\frac{1}{2}}. $$

In particular, (6.27)-(6.28) imply that the RHS of (6.26) is small, so using (2.3) we get:

$$ \big|\widetilde{\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v)\lesssim\partial_{v}r(u,v)\cdot\bigg|\exp\bigg(\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\frac{\Lambda}{2}\widetilde{r\gamma}(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}\bigg)-1\bigg|\lesssim e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\cdot\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\big|\widetilde{r\gamma}\big|(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}. $$

Together with (6.26), this implies (6.22) for $i+1.$ Similarly to the derivation of (6.19), we have that:

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{v}\big|\widetilde{\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\lesssim \displaystyle ve^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|\gamma(u,0)\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{i+1}+|\lambda|\cdot|u|\gamma(u,0)v^{n+2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\mathbf{x}(u) \displaystyle+\lambda^{2}|u|\gamma(u,0)v^{2n+2}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}, $$

where the first three terms follow by using (6.22) for $i+1,$ and the last two terms are the same as in (6.19). We bound the second term on the RHS of (6.30) using (6.2) as follows:

$$ \displaystyle|\lambda|\cdot|u|\gamma(u,0)v^{n+2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\mathbf{x}(u) \displaystyle\lesssim|\lambda|v^{n+1}\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}\cdot v\sqrt{e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\gamma(u,0)}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{2}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)\sqrt{e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)}du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim|\lambda|v^{n+1}\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}\cdot v\mathbf{s}(u)\lesssim|\lambda|v^{n+1}\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}. $$

Additionally, the third term on the RHS of (6.30) is bounded by the fifth term. Therefore, we can further bound the terms on the RHS of (6.30) to get for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\big|\widetilde{\theta^{2}\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\lesssim ve^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|\gamma(u,0)\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{i+1}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

Arguing as we did for (6.19) above, the RHS of (6.32) is small. We can repeat the derivation of (6.20) and use (6.32) instead of (6.19). This implies that (6.21) holds for $i+1,$ completing our induction argument.

In particular, the estimate (6.21) for $i=n$ implies that (6.14) holds. Iterating the argument used in proving (6.23)-(6.29), while starting with (6.21)-(6.22) for $i=n$ , we also get (6.15) and the desired bound for $\widetilde{r}$ in (6.16). Next, we have by (2.3), (6.2), and (6.14)-(6.16) that for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\big|\widetilde{\partial_{u}r}\big|(u,v) \displaystyle\lesssim\int_{0}^{v}\big|\widetilde{r\gamma\partial_{v}r}\big|(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\lesssim\int_{0}^{v}\bigg[\gamma(u,0)e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\big|\widetilde{r}\big|+|u|e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\big|\widetilde{\gamma}\big|+|u|\gamma(u,0)\big|\widetilde{\partial_{v}r}\big|\bigg](u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim v|u|\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|\lambda|v^{n+2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|\gamma(u,0)\Big[\mathbf{x}(u)+\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}\Big]+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}|u|\gamma(u,0) \displaystyle\lesssim v|u|\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)/2}|u|^{1/2}\gamma(u,0)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}\gamma(u,0), $$

which completes the proof of (6.17).

In order to prove (6.18), we first derive the following equation as a consequence of (2.2):

$$ \partial_{v}\big(\sqrt{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big)=-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{r}}\partial_{u}r\partial_{v}\phi=-\frac{1}{2r}\partial_{u}r\partial_{v}r\cdot\theta. $$

We use this to get an equation for $\partial_{v}\big(\widetilde{\sqrt{r}\partial_{u}\phi}\big)$ . Thus, we start with the following bound:

$$ \big|\widetilde{\sqrt{r}\partial_{u}\phi}\big|(u,v)\lesssim\int_{0}^{v}\bigg(|u|^{-1}\big|\widetilde{\partial_{v}r}\cdot\theta\big|+e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{-2}\big|\widetilde{r}\cdot\theta\big|+e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{-1}\Big(\big|\widetilde{\partial_{u}r}\cdot\theta\big|+\big|\widetilde{\theta}\big|\Big)\bigg)(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}. $$

We bound the terms on the RHS of (6.33) one by one. For the first term we have using (5.11), (6.2), (6.15), and (6.31):

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{v}|u|^{-1}\big|\widetilde{\partial_{v}r}\cdot\theta\big|(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\lesssim \displaystyle v|u|^{-1/2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\sqrt{\gamma(u,0)}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|u|^{-1}|\lambda|\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}v^{n+2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\mathbf{x}(u) \displaystyle+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}|u|^{-1/2}\sqrt{\gamma(u,0)} \displaystyle\lesssim \displaystyle v|u|^{-1/2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\sqrt{\gamma(u,0)}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|u|^{-1}|\lambda|v^{n+1}. $$

Additionally, the second term on the RHS of (6.33) is bounded by the same quantity. This follows since $e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{-2}\lesssim 1$ and the RHS of (6.16) is bounded by the RHS of (6.15). For the third term on the RHS of (6.33) we use (5.11) and (6.17):

$$ \int_{0}^{v}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{-1}\big|\widetilde{\partial_{u}r}\cdot\theta\big|(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\lesssim v^{2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}\sqrt{|u|\gamma(u,0)}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|\lambda|v^{n+2}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}|u|^{-1/2}\sqrt{\gamma(u,0)}. $$

Finally, for the fourth term on the RHS of (6.33) we use the bootstrap assumption (6.9):

$$ \int_{0}^{v}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{-1}\big|\widetilde{\theta}\big|(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\lesssim\sqrt{v}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u)}|u|^{-1}\bigg(\int_{0}^{v}\big|\widetilde{\theta}\big|^{2}(u,v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}\bigg)^{1/2}\lesssim|u|^{-1}|\lambda|v^{n+1}. $$

Combining the estimates for the terms on the RHS of (6.33), we completed the proof of (6.18). ∎

#### 6.1.3 Improving the bootstrap assumption (6.9)

The goal of this section is to improve the bootstrap assumption (6.9) and complete the proof of Proposition 6.2. We first notice that the wave equations (2.2) and (2.3) imply:

$$ \partial_{u}\theta=-\frac{\Lambda}{2}r\gamma\theta-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{r}}\partial_{u}\phi. $$

As a result, we can derive the following equation for $\widetilde{\theta}:$

$$ \displaystyle\partial_{u}\widetilde{\theta}= \displaystyle-\frac{\Lambda}{2}r_{\lambda}\gamma_{\lambda}\widetilde{\theta}+Err, \displaystyle Err= \displaystyle-\frac{\Lambda}{2}\widetilde{r\gamma}\cdot\theta-\frac{1}{2}\widetilde{r^{-1/2}\partial_{u}\phi}. $$

We integrate equation (6.34) to obtain for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \widetilde{\theta}(u,v)=e^{\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u,v)}\cdot\bigg(\widetilde{\theta}(u_{0},v)+\int_{u_{0}}^{u}Err\cdot e^{-\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u^{\prime},v)}(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}\bigg). $$

The essential point that allows us to improve the bootstrap assumption (6.9) is that the main contribution in (6.36) comes from the first term, determined by the initial data perturbation (6.1). We deal with the second term in (6.36) using Lemma 6.2 below. We assume for now the bound (6.37) and complete the proof of Proposition 6.2.

Combining (6.36) and (6.37), we get using (6.12) that for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\Big|\widetilde{\theta}(u,v^{\prime})-e^{\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u,v^{\prime})}\widetilde{\theta}(u_{0},v^{\prime})\Big|^{2}dv^{\prime}\lesssim\int_{0}^{v}e^{2\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u,v^{\prime})}\bigg(\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\big|Err(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})\big|e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\bigg)^{2}dv^{\prime}\lesssim\lambda^{2}v^{2n+\frac{3}{2}}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u)}. $$

We denote the implicit constant in this estimate by $C>0,$ which depends on $k,n,|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,$ and $\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$

On the other hand, we have by the definition (6.1) that $\big|\widetilde{\theta}(u_{0},v)\big|=|\lambda|v^{n}$ . We also use (6.12) to get for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{v}\big|\widetilde{\theta}(u,v^{\prime})\big|^{2}dv^{\prime}\leq \displaystyle 2\int_{0}^{v}\Big|\widetilde{\theta}(u,v^{\prime})-e^{\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u,v^{\prime})}\widetilde{\theta}(u_{0},v^{\prime})\Big|^{2}dv^{\prime}+2\int_{0}^{v}\Big|e^{\mathbf{b}_{\lambda}(u,v^{\prime})}\widetilde{\theta}(u_{0},v^{\prime})\Big|^{2}dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle 2C\lambda^{2}v^{2n+\frac{3}{2}}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u)}+2\int_{0}^{v}\Big|e^{\mathbf{b}(u)}\big(1+2v^{\prime\frac{1}{4}}\big)\lambda v^{\prime n}\Big|^{2}dv^{\prime} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle 2(C+8)\lambda^{2}v^{2n+\frac{3}{2}}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u)}+4\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u)}\leq 10\lambda^{2}v^{2n+1}e^{2\mathbf{b}(u)}, $$

provided that $v_{0}^{\prime}>0$ is small enough in terms of $k,n,|\Lambda|,|u_{0}|,$ and $\Omega^{2}(u_{0},0).$ Conditioned on (6.37), this improves the bootstrap assumption (6.9), concluding the bootstrap argument. We notice that in the above argument we also established (6.6) (again, by taking $v_{0}^{\prime}>0$ sufficiently small), which was the remaining bound in Proposition 6.2.

In the above, we completed the proof of Proposition 6.2, conditioned on (6.37). We now establish this bound to complete our argument.

#### Lemma 6.2.

Under the bootstrap assumptions (6.7)-(6.9), the error term (6.35) satisfies the following bound for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \int_{0}^{v}\bigg(\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\big|Err(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})\big|e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\bigg)^{2}dv^{\prime}\lesssim\lambda^{2}v^{2n+\frac{3}{2}}. $$

#### Proof.

Using the definition (6.35), we bound $Err$ as follows:

$$ \big|Err\big|(u,v)\lesssim|u|^{-1}\big|\widetilde{\sqrt{r}\partial_{u}\phi}\big|(u,v)+|u|^{-\frac{3}{2}}\big|\widetilde{r}\cdot\partial_{u}\phi\big|(u,v)+\big|\widetilde{r\gamma}\cdot\theta\big|(u,v). $$

Upon integration as on the LHS of (6.37), the bound (6.38) gives rise to three error terms, which we denote by $I,II,$ and $III.$ In order to bound $I,$ we use (5.6), (6.2), and (6.18):

$$ \displaystyle\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-1}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\big|\widetilde{\sqrt{r}\partial_{u}\phi}\big|(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\bigg(|u^{\prime}|^{-\frac{3}{2}}e^{-2\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\sqrt{\gamma(u^{\prime},0)}v\big[v\mathbf{s}(u^{\prime})\big]^{n}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}|u^{\prime}|^{-2}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\bigg)du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim v\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{n}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\lesssim(\epsilon^{\prime})^{n}v^{n+\frac{9}{10}}+|\lambda|v^{n+1}\lesssim|\lambda|v^{n+\frac{1}{2}}, $$

where we also used the fact that $\epsilon^{\prime}\lesssim 1$ and $v\lesssim\lambda^{4}.$ We square this relation and integrate in $v$ to get that $I$ is bounded by the RHS of (6.37).

In order to bound $II,$ we first notice that (5.12) implies for any $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle\bigg(\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-\frac{3}{2}}e^{-\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\big|\widetilde{r}\partial_{u}\phi\big|(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}\bigg)^{2} \displaystyle\lesssim\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|\gamma^{-1}(u^{\prime},0)\big|\partial_{u}\phi\big|^{2}(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}\cdot\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-4}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)e^{-2\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\big|\widetilde{r}\big|^{2}du^{\prime} \displaystyle\lesssim\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-4}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)e^{-2\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\big|\widetilde{r}\big|^{2}(u^{\prime},v)du^{\prime}. $$

We use (6.16), which creates three error terms that we bound using (6.2), (6.31) as follows:

$$ \int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-4}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)e^{-4\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}v^{2}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u^{\prime})\big]^{2n+2}du^{\prime}\lesssim v^{2}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{2n+2}\lesssim\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}, $$

$$ \lambda^{2}v^{2n+4}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-4}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)e^{-4\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\mathbf{x}^{2}(u^{\prime})du^{\prime}\lesssim\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-5}e^{-2\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\lesssim\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}\big|\log|u|\big|\lesssim\lambda^{2}v^{2n+\frac{3}{2}}, $$

$$ \int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-4}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)e^{-2\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\lambda^{4}v^{4n+4}du^{\prime}\lesssim\lambda^{2}v^{2n+3}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-3}\gamma^{2}(u^{\prime},0)e^{-4\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}du^{\prime}\lesssim\lambda^{2}v^{2n+3}. $$

Integrating in $v$ and summing these terms, we get that $II$ is bounded by the RHS of (6.37).

The last step of the proof if to bound $III.$ We have by Cauchy-Schwarz that:

$$ III\lesssim\int_{u_{0}}^{u}\int_{0}^{v}|u^{\prime}|\theta^{2}(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}du^{\prime}\cdot\sup_{v^{\prime}\in[0,v]}\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{-1}e^{-2\mathbf{b}(u^{\prime})}\big|\widetilde{r\gamma}\big|^{2}(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})du^{\prime}. $$

For the first term, we have according to (5.11) and (6.2):

$$ \int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|\int_{0}^{v}\theta^{2}(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})dv^{\prime}du^{\prime}\lesssim v\int_{u_{0}}^{u}|u^{\prime}|^{2}\gamma(u^{\prime},0)du^{\prime}\lesssim v\mathbf{s}(u)\lesssim v^{1/2}. $$

In order to deal with the second term in (6.39), we use (6.24) for $i=n$ (which follows by (6.14) and (6.16)) to get for $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :

$$ \displaystyle e^{-2\mathbf{b}(u)}\big|\widetilde{r\gamma}\big|^{2}(u,v)\lesssim \displaystyle v^{2}|u|^{4}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{2n}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}|u|^{3}\gamma(u,0)+\lambda^{4}v^{4n+2}|u|^{2}\gamma^{2}(u,0)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+4}e^{-2\mathbf{b}(u)}\mathbf{x}^{2}(u) \displaystyle\lesssim \displaystyle v^{2}|u|^{4}\big[v\mathbf{s}(u)\big]^{2n}+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+2}|u|^{3}\gamma(u,0)+\lambda^{4}v^{4n+2}|u|^{2}\gamma^{2}(u,0)+\lambda^{2}v^{2n+4}|u|\mathbf{s}^{2}(u). $$

Additionally, we use (6.2) as well to get for all $(u,v)\in[u_{0},\tilde{u}]\times[0,\tilde{v}]$ :
